Seeing Him, 'I saw and worshipped the lotus feet of the Lord with matted locks adorned with pure, soft Konrai flowers,' he sang a Thiruppathigam that rules the heavens, a garland of powerful Tamil verses beginning with 'Valvai'. He then proceeded to Thiruedhirkolpadi, surrounded by fragrant flower gardens. As he went, he sang a Thiruppathigam expressing his resolve, 'Let us reach Thiruedhirkolpadi, where the Lord with the elephant-like strength is praised and worshipped in all directions.' Having arrived, he worshipped the rich and grand temple, bowed to the Lord, stayed there, received His grace, and reached Thiruvelvikudi. There, he praised the Lord who grants liberation, singing a Thiruppathigam beginning with 'Mooppathillai' (There is no old age) in Thiruthuruthi." Thus, the 5 verses conclude.

He reached Thirukkaruppariyaloor, the temple of the Lord who kicked Yama, worshipped the temple tower, entered, and surrounded by devotees, with great devotion, he bowed and praised. With boundless joy filling his heart, he praised and came out, staying in that town. Recalling the holy Lord and speaking of the joy that comes from it, he adorned himself with the Tamil garland of Thiruppathigam beginning with 'Simmandhu' and stayed there. The Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal for Thirukkaruppariyaloor is the 30th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai (collection of hymns). The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Simmandhu simbuliththu sindhaiyinil vaithu ugandhu thirambavannam kaimavin urivaip porththu umai veruva kandanai karuppariyaloor koimavin malarcholai kuyil pada mayiladum kogudikkoyil emmanai manaththinal ninainthabodhu avar namakku iniyavare." "Kalaimalintha thenpulaivar katrortham idarthirkkum karuppariyaloor kulaimalintha kol thengu mattu ozhugum pooncholai kogudikkoyil ilaimalintha mazhuvanai manaththinal anbu seythu inbam eythi malaimalintha tholvooran vanappagai appan uraiththa vanthamizhgale." Thiruchitrambalam.

Thirukkaruppariyaloor is the 27th shrine on the northern bank of the Kaveri River, in the Chola country. It is also known as Melaikkazhi Thalaignayiru. Kogudikkoyil is the name of the temple. The temple history states that once, Indra, filled with arrogance, went to Kailash. When the Lord appeared before him in the form of a Yaksha, Indra, unknowingly, launched his Vajrayudha (thunderbolt) at Him. Realizing his mistake, he bowed and worshipped, and to atone for his fault, he came here, worshipped the Lord, and received blessings. The Lord's name is Kutram Poruthanathar (Lord who forgives sins), and the Goddess's name is Kolvalai Nayaki. This place can be reached a short distance west from Thiruppunkur, then reaching Mannippallam, and from there a short distance north.

Having worshipped Thirukkaruppariyaloor and received the Lord's grace, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal reached Thiruppazhamannippadikkari, a fertile land where carp leap in the water. There, he bowed to the lotus feet of the Lord, who shares His body with Uma, praised Him, and sang a Thiruppathigam of countless glories, beginning with 'Munnavan'. Thus, he worshipped the Lord. The Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal for Thiruppazhamannippadikkari is the 22nd Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Nattaraga Pann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Munnavan engal piran mudhal kanbu arithaya piran senniyil engal piran thiru neelamidatru empiran manni engal piran marai nankum kallal nizhal keezh panniya engal piran pazhamanni padikkaraiye." "Palvuyir vazhum thenneer pazhamanni padikkaraiyai alli antha marai thar arooran uraiththa thamil solluthal kettal vallar avarkkum thamarkkum kilaikkum elliyum nanpagalum idarkooruthal illai anre." Thiruchitrambalam.

The Lord's abode is Pazhamannippadikkari. Sekkizhar Peruman praises this as a Thiruppathigam of countless glories because it describes the Lord's attributes and urges devotees to reach and worship Him. Thiruppazhamannippadikkari is the 30th shrine on the northern bank of the Kaveri River in the Chola country. It is also known as Izhaippaippattu. The temple history states that when the Lord consumed poison, the Goddess prevented it from going down further by holding His throat, thus revealing His blue throat (Thiruneelakandam). The Lord's name is Thiruneelakandar, and the Goddess's name is Amirthakaravalli. We can see the Lord's name praised as 'Thiruneelamizhatru Empiran' in the Thiruppathigam. It is reachable a short distance from Vaidheeswaran Koil.

Having worshipped Thiruppazhamannippadikkari, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal continued his pilgrimage. At that time, he suddenly remembered that Thiruvazhkozhiputhur was nearby and that he was passing by without worshipping there. So, he turned back, reached Thiruvazhkozhiputhur, praised the Lord, and sang a Thiruppathigam. Geographically, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal was going west from Thirukkaruppariyaloor to Pazhamannippadikkari. It is customary and a duty of pilgrimage to worship the shrines that fall in between. However, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, while going from Thirukkaruppariyaloor to Pazhamannippadikkari, passed Thiruvazhkozhiputhur without worshipping it. After going some distance, he remembered Thiruvazhkozhiputhur, returned, and sang a Thiruppathigam, with the refrain "Vazhkozhiputhur manikkaththai marandhu en ninaikkene" (Why do I think of anything else, having forgotten the gem of Vazhkozhiputhur?) in each verse.

The Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal for Thiruvazhkozhiputhur is the 57th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Thakkesi Pann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Thalaikkalan thalaimel thariththanai thannai ennai ninaikka tharuvanaik kolaik yanai uriporththu ugandanai kootruthaiththa kuraiser kazhalanai alaiththa senkan vidaiyeravallanai anaiyal adiyen adinayen malaiththa sennal vayal vazhkozhiputhur manikkaththai marandhu en ninaikkene." "Valankizhar pozhil vazhkozhiputhur manikkaththai marandhu en ninaikken endru ulankulir thamil ooran vanthondan sadaiyan kadhalan vanappagai appan nalankizhar vayal navalar vendhan nangai singadi thanthai payantha palankizhar thamil padavallar mel paraiyumam seytha pavangalthane." Thiruchitrambalam.

The Lord's name in Thiruvazhkozhiputhur is Manikkavannar, and the Goddess's name is Vandamar Poonkuzhali. It is the 29th shrine on the northern bank of the Kaveri River in the Chola country. It is also known as Vazhozhithuthur and Vazhapputrur. Since it contains a Manikya Lingam worshipped by Vishnu, this shrine is called Arathanapuram in Sanskrit. We see that the Lord's name is Manikkavannar. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal also praises Him as 'Manikkaththai' in every verse of the Thiruppathigam. References to Vishnu's worship and Arjuna's worship are also found in the Thiruppathigam. The history states that Arjuna hid his sword in an anthill (putru), hence the name Vazhozhithuthur. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal has sung a Thiruppathigam of 12 verses for this shrine. The Sthala Vriksham (sacred tree) is the Vagai tree, and the Theertham (sacred water body) is Brahma Theertham.

Having sung this Thiruppathigam and reached the shrine, he bowed at the entrance of the Lord's temple, with goosebumps rising on his body, worshipped, praised, and glorified the Lord who has the daughter of the mountain king on His left side. Then, he came out and stayed there. Leaving that Thiruvazhkozhiputhur with beautiful, soft sugarcane, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal approached Thirukkanattumulloor. As he reached Thirukkanattumulloor, the Lord with the eye on His forehead appeared before Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Expressing the sentiment "I saw and worshipped the Lord adorned with pure, fresh, soft Konrai flowers," Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praised Him by adorning Him with a garland of rich Tamil verses beginning with 'Valvai', which has the power to command the celestial world.

The Thiruppathigam thus sung is the 40th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Kolli Kavuvanam Pann, and belongs to Thirukkanattumulloor. Sekkizhar Peruman praises this as "Vaan Alum Thiruppathigam" (the Thiruppathigam that rules the heavens). In this Thiruppathigam, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises the Lord as the King of the celestials, the one who swallowed and spat out the worlds, the four-faced one, the one who became the world, the one who is the five elements, the one with eight attributes, the one who is yesterday, today, and tomorrow, the jewel among the Devas, the King of the celestials, the Lord of the immortals, the one with many forms, the one who shows us the true path so that we do not sink into the fierce hell, the primordial one of the Vedas. Because Sundaramoorthy Swamigal thus describes the Lord's ultimate nature and His nature as the Lord of the Devas, Sekkizhar Peruman praises it as "Vaan Alum Thiruppathigam," meaning the Thiruppathigam that governs the celestials. In the Thirukkadaikkappu (concluding verse) of this Thiruppathigam, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal also states the benefit of the Thiruppathigam: "They themselves will stand as leaders even for the celestials."

The first and last verses of such a special Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Valvai mathimizhum valar sadaiyinanai maraiyavanai vaaimozhiyai vanavar tham konai pulvai keendulagam vizhungi umizhnthanai pon niraththin muppuri nool nan mugaththinanai mulvai madarazhuvi mudathazhai eendru mottalarnthu virainarum muruguviri pozhil soozh kalvai karunguvazhai kanvalarum kalani kanattumullooril kandu thozhuthene." "Thirainar kadal soozhntha thennilangai konai setravanai senjadai mel venmathiyinanai karainar punal thazhuvu kollidaththin karaimel kanattumullooril kandu kazhal thozhuthu urainar mathaiyanai navalar arooran urimaiyal urai seytha onthamizhgal vallar varainar vagai gnanamandavarkkum tham poy vanavarkkum thalaivaray nirpar avar thame." Thiruchitrambalam.

Thirukkanattumulloor is the 32nd shrine on the northern bank of the Kaveri River in the Chola country. It is also known as Kanattampuliyur. It is the shrine where Patanjali Muni worshipped the Lord. Therefore, the Lord's name is Patanjalinathar, and the Goddess's name is Kanar Kuzhali Kol Valai Kai Ammai. Surya Theertham and Surya Pushkarani are the sacred water bodies. The Sthala Vriksham is Vellarku. It is an ancient temple built of red bricks. An inscription from the time of Vikrama Chola mentions this shrine as Virutharaja Bhayankara Valanattu Keelkanattumulloor, also known as Thiruchitrambala Chathurvedi Mangalam. It is located a short distance southwest of Chidambaram and very close to Mannargudi.

Having worshipped Thirukkanattumulloor, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal received the Lord's grace and proceeded to Thiruedhirkolpadi. Let us continue our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 858, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkama Nayanar Puranam. Having worshipped Thirukkanattumulloor, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal received the Lord's grace and proceeded to Thiruedhirkolpadi. In Thiruedhirkolpadi, he praised the Lord and sang a Thiruppathigam beginning with 'Mathaiyanai' (The intoxicated elephant). In it, he sang a Thiruppathigam expressing his resolve, "Let us reach Thiruedhirkolpadi." This Thiruppathigam emphasizes the impermanence of the world and imprints it in our minds. Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman praises it as "Siththanilai Thiruppathigam" (Thiruppathigam of resolute state).

The Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal for Thiruedhirkolpadi is the 7th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Indalappann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Maththa yanaiyeri mannar soozha varuveergal seththa pothil arumillai sindhaiyul vaimingal vaiththa ullam matra venda vammin manaththire aththar koyil edhirkolpadi enbathu adaivome." "Muththuneetru pavazhameni senjadaiyan uraiyum paththar panthaththu edhirkolpadi paramanaiye paniyasiththam vaiththa thondar thondan sadaiyan avan siruvan paththan ooran padal vallar patham panivare." Thiruchitrambalam. In this entire Thiruppathigam, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal emphasizes the impermanence of the body, wealth, and other aspects of life.

Having worshipped Thiruedhirkolpadi, he worshipped the rich and grand temple, bowed to the Lord's feet, stayed in that town, received His grace, and proceeded to Thiruvelvikudi to worship Lord Shiva. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped Thiruvelvikudi and then went to Thiruthuruthi to worship the Lord. He combined the two shrines, Thiruvelvikudi and Thiruthuruthi, and sang a Thiruppathigam beginning with 'Mooppathillai' (There is no old age). That Thiruppathigam is the 18th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Nattaraga Pann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Mooppathum illai pirappathum illai irappathu illai serppathu kattagaththu oorinamaaga sinthikkin allal kappathu velvikudi than thurutthi em kon araimel arpathu nagam arinthomel nam ivarkku atpadome." "Koodalar mannan kula navaloor kon nalathamizhai padavalla paraman adiyarkku adimai valuva nadavalla thondan arooran atpadumaru solli padavallar paralogaththu iruppathu pandam anre." Thiruchitrambalam. We have already contemplated the special features of Thiruthuruthi and Thiruvelvikudi.

Thiruedhirkolpadi is the 24th shrine on the northern bank of the Kaveri River in the Chola country. It is known as Melaithirumanjeri. Thirumanjeri, the 25th shrine, is very close to it. It is said that the name Edhirkolpadi came from the history of the Lord going to meet and escort a prince, who was a devotee, in the guise of a father-in-law. It is a shrine where Airavatham worshipped and received blessings. The Lord's name is Airavatheeswarar, and the Goddess's name is Malarkozhil Nayaki.

Now, the 122nd and 123rd verses: "Having worshipped the beautiful wedding form of the Lord in Thiruvelvikudi with devotion in his heart, Nambi Aroorar praised Him. Surrounded by ascetics, he departed from there, filled with love. He worshipped the many shrines where the Lord had taken him as His own, and then, with boundless love, accompanied by the devotees, he praised the many abodes of the Lord with the poison-stained throat. Surrounded by flower gardens where clouds gather and lotus ponds, he reached Thiruvarur, with its rich paddy fields and fertile lands." These are the verses.

In Thiruvelvikudi, the Lord is in the form of a bridegroom, known as Kalyana Sundarar. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped that beautiful wedding form of the Lord with devotion in his heart and praised Him. Surrounded by devotees who had accumulated merits through long penance, he departed from there. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped many shrines where the Lord, bound by love, had taken him as His own. The companions were devotees who had accumulated merits through penance, devotees who had performed great penance over many births. It is implied here that only such steadfast devotees could have the privilege of being surrounded by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and worshipping him. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, accompanied by such devotees who possessed boundless and unwavering love, worshipped and praised many abodes of the Lord. These shrines include Thiruazhundhur, Thiruazhuvur, Thirumeeysur, Thiruthilathaipathimutram, Thiruambar Maganam, Thiruambar Perunthirukkoil, Thirukkondeeswaram, Thiruvirkudi, Thiruppalliyin Mukkoodal, and others.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal undertook a very long pilgrimage. Therefore, he decided to go from Thiruvelvikudi to Thiruvarur and continued that journey. The shrines mentioned above are those that fell on his way to Thiruvarur. He praised all these shrines and reached Thiruvarur. We do not have the Thiruppathigams sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal for these shrines. Having worshipped many such abodes, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal reached Thiruvarur, which is surrounded by flower gardens where clouds gather, and lotus ponds, with abundant fertile lands. The verses here describe the water resources, land fertility, and other glories of Thiruvarur. It is described that clouds surround the gardens, the gardens enclose the lotus ponds, and these ponds, being numerous, surround the fields. Thus, Thiruvarur is surrounded by fertile lands rich in fields.

Now, the next verse, the 124th verse: "In the prosperous Thiruvarur, where Devas and sages gather, they came to the grand temple tower, worshipped, and entered. With boundless love, they raised their hands in supplication, and with many devotees, they approached the Lord." Thiruvarur is specifically spoken of as "Selvamali Thiruvarur" (Thiruvarur rich in wealth). Here, wealth refers to both worldly wealth and the wealth of liberation. We previously saw the explanation of the name Thiruvarur as "Thiru Arkindra Oor" (the town where prosperity abounds). Such is Thiruvarur, rich in wealth. There, Devas and sages gather at the grand temple tower, the Devasiriya Thirumandapam. The devotees gathered in the temple, along with the devotees accompanying Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, all together, with boundless love, raised their hands above their heads and, accompanied by many devotees, approached the Lord.

The 125th verse: "The Lord, who is the beginningless, middleless, and endless primordial one, who has the bull banner, is enshrined in Thirumoolattanaththu. With unending great love, he worshipped Him and came out. He then reached the mansion of Paravaiyar, whose fame is unwavering." The Lord is always full of divine qualities, without beginning, middle, or end. He is enshrined in Thirumoolattanaththu in Thiruvarur. One can see the Lord, who is everywhere, manifested in Thirumoolattanaththu. Thirumoolattanam in Thiruvarur is the place where Vanmeeganathar, the Lord who resides in the anthill, is enshrined. It is said that he worshipped the Lord "in Thirumoolattanaththu," not "Thirumoolattanaththu Iraivar" (the Lord of Thirumoolattanam). This implies that the one supreme Lord Shiva, who is omnipresent, is enshrined here in Thirumoolattanam, and also in Thirumuthukundram, and in many other shrines in the form of Linga manifestations and in temples. This refers to the fact that he received gold in Thirumuthukundram, released it into the river, and is now going to retrieve that gold from the Thiruvarur tank by the grace of the Lord. Thus, this verse is structured with that implication.

Having worshipped the Lord, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal came out of the temple. The first duty upon reaching a shrine is to worship the Lord in the temple before doing anything else. This was the practice of the elders in ancient times, the path shown to us by them. We are reminded here of the history of Sivapatha Hrudayar, who, upon reaching Madurai, first worshipped Lord Sokkanathar in Thirualavai before going to the monastery where Thirugnanasambandha Peruman resided. Unlike this, nowadays, some people, upon reaching a shrine, first attend to all other matters and only then go to the temple. This is very regrettable. Having worshipped the Lord and come out of the temple, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal proceeded to Paravai Nachiyar's mansion. Let us continue our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 859, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkama Nayanar Puranam. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal arrived in Thiruvarur, worshipped Vanmeeganathar (the Lord who resides in the anthill), and then proceeded to Paravaiyar's mansion. Four verses, 126, 127, 128, and 129, follow consecutively. They are as follows: "With surging great love, he bowed at the feet of Paravaiyar, whose lotus eyes and red fruit-like lips were praised by many women with flowing tresses. She sweetly said, 'You have remembered even us,' and with that beautiful lady, he stayed happily. On those days, the Nayanar said, 'The good treasure given to us by the Lord of Muthukundram, we cast it into the pure Manimutharu River. By His grace, go and retrieve it from the tank on the western side of His temple's mansion, and bring it.' When he said this, she, with her lightning-like waist, smiled faintly and said, 'What a wonder is this! What are you saying?' He, who knew the truth, said, 'By the grace of my Lord, I will retrieve the gold from the tank and give it to you. It will not be false.' As she also accompanied him, with boundless joy, they entered and worshipped the ancient Lord who rejoices within the beautiful temple. They circumambulated the grand temple mansion and then went to the beautiful tank on the western side, accompanied by Paravaiyar, his unique companion."

When Sundaramoorthy Swamigal arrived at Paravaiyar's mansion, Paravai Ammaiyar came and bowed at Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's feet, saying, "Are we worthy of your grace, that you have remembered even us and come here?" Paravai Nachiyar meant, "You, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, whose heart thinks of none other than Lord Shiva, have remembered even us, who are not worthy of being remembered, and have come here. Are we worthy of such grace?" Thus, Paravai Ammaiyar bowed at Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's feet. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal spoke sweet words to Paravai Ammaiyar, and on a day when they were happily together, he said, "Lord Shiva, who is our Lord and resides in Thirumuthukundram, bestowed upon us a good treasure of gold. We cast that gold into the Manimutharu River in Virudhachalam. By the grace of Lord Shiva, we will go and retrieve that gold from the Kamalalayam tank, which is on the western side of His temple's mansion in Thiruvarur. You also come with me."

Sekkizhar Peruman refers to the gold given by the Lord as "Nannidhiyam" (good treasure), even though gold is a product of Maya. Although this gold is a material object of impure Maya, it is a divine gift received from the Lord, and therefore it becomes a beneficial good treasure. The Lord of Thirumuthukundram, who resides in Virudhachalam, is the same Lord who resides in the beautiful temple in Thiruvarur. There, in Thirumuthukundram, the Lord said, "Cast it into the Manimutharu River and retrieve it from the Thiruvarur tank." Accordingly, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal cast the gold into the river there. Therefore, it is now the Lord's duty to return that gold in the Thiruvarur tank as He had promised.

When Sundaramoorthy Swamigal said this, Paravai Nachiyar was greatly astonished. She said with a faint smile, "What a wonder is this! What a miracle!" Then Sundaramoorthy Swamigal said, "O lady with a beautiful forehead! By the grace of my Lord, I will retrieve all the gold from this tank and give it to you. It will not be false." Paravai Nachiyar's faint smile was a hint of sarcasm. Even though Paravai Nachiyar said, "What a wonder! What a miracle!" it was as if she spoke like those who doubt the Lord's grace. Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal said, "I will retrieve the gold that my Lord gave us from the tank and give it to you." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal also said, "You yourself accept that gold in your hand and serve ambrosia to the devotees during the Panguni Uthiram festival." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal also said that he would give all 12,000 gold coins without any reduction.

Having said this, as Paravai Ammaiyar also accompanied Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, with boundless joy, they entered and worshipped the holy Lord who rejoices within the beautiful temple of Thiruvarur. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal circumambulated the grand temple mansion of Thiruvarur. From there, he proceeded to the Kamalalayam tank, which is on the western side of the Thiruvarur temple. We can contemplate here the ideas from the 10th Sutra of Sivagnanabodham: "He does nothing without His grace," and "He stands as one, ever in the Lord's service." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal says, "By His grace, I will go and retrieve it," and "By the grace of my Lord, I will retrieve it from the tank and give it to you." These statements remind us of the ideas in that 10th Sutra. It is a proven truth that Nambigal (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal) was a supreme Acharya who was completely devoid of self-assertion and was inextricably merged in the Lord's grace. Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal proceeded to the Kamalalayam tank, which is on the western side of the Thiruvarur temple, accompanied by Paravai Nachiyar.

Now, six verses, 130, 131, 132, 133, 134, and 135, describe the subsequent divine event, as narrated by Sekkizhar Peruman. Those verses are as follows: "He came to the northeastern bank of the tank, made the young lady stand there, and the Lord of Munaippadi, with matted locks, worshipped the Lord and descended into the tank. As if he were putting it in and taking it out on that very day, he searched there. The Lord, beautiful with sacred ash, was pleased with his song and, in His divine play, did not bring the pure gold into the tank. 'What is this grace, that you cast it into the river and search for it in the tank?' asked the lady with bangles. As the unique devotee, following the grace he had received before, without a smile appearing on Paravai's beautiful, fragrant lips, he said, 'Give it to me.' He then sang a Thiruppathigam praising the Lord, 'O Brahmin with the sacred thread on your chest, O Lord with a body of gold, who resides in Muthukundram.' Even after eight verses, the gold that the celestials know was given in Muthukundram did not appear, and he was distressed by its absence. He sang the verse, 'Give me the gold that I cast, in front of her.' Even after eight verses, the gold did not appear. He sang the verse, 'I have never failed to praise you.' He prayed to the Lord with the eye on His forehead, who dances in the cosmic hall, protecting all worlds, 'O Dancer, grant it in front of this tender lady.' As he, who stood on a path unknown even to ascetics, prayed, by the grace of the Lord who dances with Konrai flowers on His head, a heap of gold emerged. He retrieved it in due order. Flowers rained from the sky, and the people on earth worshipped, saying, 'What a wonder is this! Who else can receive such a blessing?'"

Thus, the six verses conclude. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, with Paravai Nachiyar, reached the northeastern bank of the Kamalalayam tank in Thiruvarur. He made Paravaiyar stand on the bank, worshipped the Lord, and descended into the tank. He searched there as if he were putting in and taking out the 12,000 gold coins. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal searched on the northeastern bank. This northeastern bank of Kamalalayam is the bank that is on the northeastern side if one comes through the western gopuram (tower) entrance of the Thiruvarur temple. The northeast is considered the direction of Ishana, which holds great significance. Currently, there is a shrine for Maatruraiththa Pillaiyar (Pillaiyar who verified the purity of gold) there. This Pillaiyar is enshrined here with a name related to this story. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is entering into a great act where the Lord's grace is about to manifest. Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worships the Lord specifically before entering. We see this in the history of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and in the history of great Acharyas.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal searches as if to retrieve the 12,000 gold coins. The Lord, beautiful with sacred ash, is very pleased with Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's songs. Therefore, due to His divine play, wanting to receive Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's Thiruppathigam, He did not bring the 12,000 gold coins into the tank. Lord Shiva, beautiful with sacred ash, thus delays the appearance of the gold. Sacred ash signifies dissolution. After dissolution, re-creation occurs. Similarly, the gold that disappeared will be given again. The Lord desires to hear the sweet Thiruppathigam sung by Nambigal. Therefore, Lord Shiva delays for a short while, engaging in this divine play, in order to hear Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's Thiruppathigam.

As the Lord delayed, Paravai Ammaiyar, who had previously smiled with a hint of sarcasm, now confirmed it again, saying, "Did you cast it into the river and are now searching for it in the tank?" Paravai spoke, incorporating the proverb "searching in the tank after casting into the river." The underlying meaning of Paravai Ammaiyar's statement is that it is a futile act. An object cast into a river cannot be found even if searched for in the same spot in the river. In such a situation, casting it into a river in Virudhachalam (Thirumuthukundram) and searching for it in a completely different place, a tank in Thiruvarur, is an impossible task. Thus, Paravai Ammaiyar asks, "Are you searching in the tank after casting it into the river?" Here, the river refers to the Manimutharu River in Thirumuthukundram, and the tank refers to the Kamalalayam tank in Thiruvarur. This makes it a very apt occasion for Paravaiyar's laughter. Paravaiyar asks, "You said you would receive this by the Lord's grace. Is this how the Lord's grace manifests for us?" Paravai Ammaiyar asks and laughs.

Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal requests the Lord. With the intention that Paravaiyar should not laugh, "O Lord, please grant the gold as you graced me in Thirumuthukundram," Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, wearing the sacred thread on his chest, sings a Thiruppathigam beginning with "O Lord, whose body is like gold, who resides in Thirumuthukundram." The Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is the 25th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Nattaraga Pann. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal continues to sing the verses of this Thiruppathigam. Even after singing eight verses, the 12,000 gold coins did not appear. Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal sings the ninth verse, beginning with "Yen Imaihor" (Why the celestials). Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prays, "O Lord with the eye on your forehead, the great Dancer in the cosmic hall who protects all worlds, please grant the 12,000 gold coins in front of this tender Paravai." He is one who stands on a path unknown even to ascetics.

The first, ninth, and last verses of the Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Pon seytha meniyineer puli tholai araikkasaiththeer mun seytha mooveyilum eriththeer muthukundru amarnththeer min seytha nun idaiyal paravai ival than mugappe en seythavaaru adikel adiyen ittalam kedave." "Eththathu irunthariyene imaiyor thani nayakane mooththay ulagukku ellam muthukundram amarnthavane pooththarum kuzhalal paravai ival than mugappe kooththa thanthu arulvay kodiyen ittalam kedave." "Piraiyarum sadayam peruman arulay endru muraiyal vanthu amarar vanangum muthukundrar thammai maraiyarththam kurisil vayal naval arooran sonna iraiyar padal vallarkku elitham sivalogamathhe." Thiruchitrambalam.

At that time, by the grace of the Lord, the divine Dancer adorned with Konrai flowers, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal received the heap of 12,000 gold coins. He took it and came ashore. Flowers rained from the celestial world. All the people on earth worshipped, saying, "What a wonder is this!" They worshipped, saying, "Who else but Sundaramoorthy Swamigal can receive such divine grace? No one else." This is the Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal as if reminding the Lord in a friendly way, "You gave an ethereal voice in Thirumuthukundram, which was heard not only by kings but also by celestials. Therefore, you cannot refuse to give this. You cannot deny it."

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal receiving gold from the Lord, casting it into the river there and retrieving it from the tank here, and singing with Paravai Nachiyar as the focus—all these should not be misunderstood by worldly people as attachment to gold and women, leading to offenses. Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman praises Sundaramoorthy Swamigal as "Neeththarum thodarvariya neri nindrar" (one who stood on a path unknown even to ascetics), meaning that he stood on the path of Shiva, which is difficult even for ascetics of severe penance to follow. Thus, Sekkizhar Peruman praises him. Having received the 12,000 gold coins, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal came ashore. Lord Shiva continues His divine play.

The 136th verse: "Having retrieved the good gold, which brought forth divine knowledge, and as the Lord with the blue throat, by His grace, delayed in giving the purity of the gold, the devotee praised the feet of the Lord, who is difficult for Vishnu and Brahma to reach." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, having retrieved the 12,000 gold coins and come ashore, to the astonishment of all the people of the world, checked the purity of the gold. We have already seen that before casting the gold into the river in Thirumuthukundram, he cut off a small portion and kept it with him. So, when he compared the gold he now received from the tank, by the grace of Lord Shiva, the gold from the tank was of lower purity. Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal again praised Lord Shiva.

Gold is a material object born of Maya, which can lead to the delusion of Maya and rebirth. We should recall here the history of Aludaiya Arasugal Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who, in the courtyard of Thiruppukalur, did not even touch the pure gold and precious gems that came by divine grace. He carried them in his sacred hoe and cast them into the beautiful lotus pond. There, the Lord, revealing the good state of Arasugal to the world, blessed him so that gold and gems appeared wherever Thirunavukkarasu Peruman used his hoe. Through that divine grace, the true state of Arasugal's goodness was established, and the world came to know it and attain salvation. Here, the Panguni Uthiram festival is approaching in Thiruvarur. This gold was received by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal from the Lord to prepare sacred food for the devotees on that festival day. He cast it into the river and retrieved it from the tank. Therefore, this becomes a good treasure, because it is gold given by the Lord to feed sacred food to the pure devotees of Lord Shiva. Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman refers to it as "Narkanagam" (good gold) in this verse.

When an object received by divine grace is cast into a river and retrieved from a tank by divine grace, it is not to be assumed that it will be returned exactly as it was, without any reduction in purity. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, having cut off a small piece of gold and kept it with him to check its purity, caused Lord Shiva to now make the gold of lower purity. We are reminded here of the Thiruvandap Paguthi of Thiruvachagam: "To those who thought, 'We will see in this trick,' He removed that trick." Now, due to the Lord's divine play, He delayed the appearance of the gold, so Sundaramoorthy Swamigal sang a song. Similarly, here, when the Lord, by His grace, made the gold of lower purity, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal again praised the Lord and sang a Thiruppathigam.

Now, the 137th verse: "When he praised Him again, the Lord, who rejoices in songs born of true love, accepted it. The gold, which had a defect, became pure, without any flaw, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal took it and came ashore." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal again praised the Lord. The Lord, who rejoices in songs born of true love, accepted it. The defect in the gold was removed, and He gave pure gold to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal without any flaw. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal took it and came ashore. It is understood that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, who had been standing on the steps of the northeastern part of the tank until then, now came ashore. Correspondingly, the temple of Maatruraiththa Pillaiyar is also located in the northeastern part of the tank.

The 138th verse: "Having come ashore with Paravaiyar, he had all the gold carried by many people to the tall mansion. He then worshipped the fragrant lotus feet of the Lord of Thirumoolattanam, whose matted locks bear the flowing waters, and reached the street." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, having come ashore, sent all the gold, which were gold ingots, to Paravai Ammaiyar's mansion. He had them carried as a burden by people and sent them to Paravai Ammaiyar. Then, he went to worship the lotus-like feet of Vanmeeganathar, who resides in Thirumoolattanesvarar in Thiruvarur. He came to worship Thirumoolattanesvarar to retrieve the gold. Now, having received the gold, when he returned, he worshipped Thirumoolattana Nathar and came to the street outside the Lord's temple, the street that leads to Paravai Ammaiyar's mansion, which is outside the southern entrance of the beautiful temple.

The 139th verse: "Having entered the mansion, as the sound of endless auspicious blessings rose in abundance, the protector of the people of Thiruvarur, with fragrant flower gardens, sat with the beautiful lady, filled with joy." Having arrived at the street on the southern side of the temple, he entered Paravai Ammaiyar's mansion. As the sound of endless auspicious blessings, offered by countless people, resounded there, Nambigal Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, the protector of the people of Thirunavalur, with fragrant flower gardens, sat with Paravaiyar in the mansion, filled with heartfelt joy. Let us continue our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 860, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkama Nayanar Puranam. The 140th and 141st verses: "On a certain day, he worshipped the Supreme Being residing in the beautiful anthill of Thiruvarur. He sang a Thiruppathigam praising Him, with unending bliss overflowing. With the devotees, he inquired about the resolute truth, worshipped, danced, and sang. He began with 'Paaru Thaangi' (He who bears the earth), and with overflowing joy in his heart, goosebumps rose on his body, tears filled his eyes, and boundless bliss appeared in countless ways. He praised, rejoiced, and was filled with happiness."

On that day, when Sundaramoorthy Swamigal was residing in Thiruvarur, he regularly worshipped Vanmeeganathar, the Lord who resides in the beautiful anthill of Thiruvarur. At that time, he praised the Lord and sang a Thiruppathigam. In that Thiruppathigam, with unending bliss overflowing, he, along with the devotees, inquired about the resolute truths of the Lord's great grace in various ways, and thus sang the Thiruppathigam. Singing by mingling with devotees and asking questions about the Lord's greatness as if he did not know them is one of the most excellent ways to immerse oneself in divine grace. The 12th Sutra of Sivagnanabodham states, "Anbarudu Mariyi" (mingling with devotees). This is spoken of as one of the characteristics of Jivanmuktas (liberated souls). We can see this characteristic in the Thirukkandiyur Pillaiyar Thiruppathigam and in the Thiruppathigams sung when he first arrived in Thiruvarur, where he prioritized the devotees. We should remember that Thiruvarur is a shrine famous for its devotion.

Thus, he sang a Thiruppathigam. It was a Thiruppathigam that began with 'Paaru Thaangi' (He who bears the earth), perfectly set to music. With overflowing joy in his heart, goosebumps rose on his body, tears filled his eyes, and boundless bliss appeared in countless ways. He praised, rejoiced, and was filled with happiness. It was set to the tune of Kollippenn. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Paaru thaangiya kaadaro paduthalaiyaro malai pavai oor kooru thaangiya kuzhagaro kulaikkatha kurungottu ila eru thaangiya kodiyaro sudupodiyaro ilankum pirai aru thaangiya sadaiyaro namakku adigalagiya adigale." "Padisai neermayin bhakthargal paninthu ethinen paniyeer arulvadiyilan thirunavaluran vanappagai appan vanthondan sediyanagilum theeyanagilum thammaiye manam sinthikkum adiyan uranai azhvaro namakku adigalagiya adigale." Thiruchitrambalam.

Now, the 142nd verse: "On those days of joyful residence, having received the grace of the King adorned with snakes in the strong anthill, praised by the endless Vedas, he departed with loving devotion to worship the Lord with shining matted locks in countless other shrines." On those days when he resided there with joy and devotion, having received the grace of the Lord who resides in the anthill in Thiruvarur, praised and glorified by the Vedas, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal departed with boundless love and devotion to worship the Lord with shining matted locks in countless other shrines.

"With his retinue accompanying him, in every suitable shrine, he worshipped the feet of the Lord who wears the elephant hide, rejoiced, and praised Him. The pure and great devotee, Nambigal, proceeded to worship Thirunallar, where true devotees, who never forget Shiva, came to receive him." This is the 143rd verse. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal departed from Thiruvarur, accompanied by his retinue, his servants. He visited nearby shrines such as Thiruvilamar, Thiruppalliyin Mukkoodal, and others. He worshipped the feet of the Lord who wears the elephant hide, rejoiced, and praised Him. The pure and great devotee, Nambigal, proceeded to worship many shrines and reached Thirunallar. As Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, intending to worship Thirunallar, proceeded, true devotees, who never forgot Shiva, came to receive him, and he entered Thirunallar.

The 144th verse: "He bowed to the sky-touching gopuram (tower), raised his hands above his head, entered, circumambulated the Lord's temple, and with surging great love, he prostrated on the ground at the lotus feet of the Lord of Thirunallar." He bowed to the sky-touching gopuram of Thirunallar temple, rose, raised his hands above his head, entered, circumambulated the temple, and with surging great love, he prostrated on the ground at the beautiful lotus feet of the steadfast Lord of Thirunallar. Having worshipped thus, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal sang a Thiruppathigam. The Thiruppathigam for Thirunallar is the 68th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Thakkesi Pann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Semponmeni venniru anivanai kariya kandanai mal ayan kanaa sambuvai thazhal angaiyinanai samavedhanai than oppu ilanai kumbama kariyin uriyanai kovin melvarum kovinai engal nambanai nallaranai amuthai nayinen maranthu en ninaikkene." "Nerinthu solaigal soozhntha nallarru em sivanai navalur singadi thanthai maranthu nan matra ninaippathu ethu endru vanappagai appan uran vanthondan sirantha malai anjinodu anjum sinthai ulvorugi seppavallarkku iranthu pokku illai varavu illai agi inba vellaththul iruppargal inithe." Thiruchitrambalam.

In the 6th verse of this Thirunallar Thiruppathigam, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal provides internal evidence of the story of the Lord taking him as His own in Thiruvannainallur, saying, "Vennainalluril arputha pazha avanam katti adiyana ennai al athu konda nalpathaththai" (He showed the wonderful ancient document in Vennainallur and took me, His servant, as His own). In the 8th verse, he praises the Lord as "Adiyenukku elivantha thuthanai thannai thozhamai aruli thondan en seytha thurisugal porukkum nathanai" (The messenger who came easily to me, who granted me friendship, the Lord who forgives the faults committed by me, His servant). In the 10th verse, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal refers to himself as Singadi Thanthai Vanappagai Appan. All these serve as internal evidence for the history of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal.

Now, the 145th and 146th verses describe the history of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal visiting Thirukkadavur Mayanam and Thirukkadavur. "Having worshipped the Lord there and received His grace, he departed and reached Thirukkadavur, with its beautiful mansions where clouds gather. He worshipped the Thirumayanam of the Lord with the moon-adorned crown and praised Him with a surging musical Thiruppathigam, beginning with 'Maruvar Konrai'. He then worshipped the feet of the Lord of Thiruveerattanam, who destroyed the fierce valor of Yama, and with great devotion, he sang a garland of Tamil verses beginning with 'Podiyar Meniyane' and proceeded to Thiruvazhamburam, the Lord who bent the mountain." Having worshipped and praised the Lord thus, and having received His grace, he departed and reached Thirukkadavur, with its beautiful mansions where clouds gather. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped the Thirumayanam shrine of the Lord and sang a Thiruppathigam beginning with 'Maruvar Konrai'.

Thirukkadavur and Thirukkadavur Mayanam are two parts of the same shrine, with temples located close to each other. Kadavur is the name of the place. Thirumayanam is a shrine there, and Veerattam is another shrine. So, Thirukkadavur Thirumayanam temple and Thirukkadavur Veerattam temple are located in Thirukkadavur. The Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praising the Lord there is the 53rd Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Pazhampanjuram Pann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Maruvar konrai mathisoodi manikkaththin malai pola varuvar vidaimel matho magizhndhu boothappadai soozha thirumal biraman indrarkkum devar nagar thanavarkkum peruman kadavur mayanaththu periya peruman adigale." "Madam malku kadavurin maraiyor eththum mayanaththu peedai theera adiyarkku arulum peruman adigal seer nadi naval arooran nambi sonna nal thamizhgal padum adiyar ketpar mel papamana paraiyume." Thiruchitrambalam.

Having worshipped Thirukkadavur Mayanam, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praised the feet of Amirthakadeswarar, the Lord of Devas, who resides in Thirukkadavur Thiruveerattanam, and the Lord enshrined there. He praised the Lord and sang a Thiruppathigam beginning with 'Podiyar Meniyane'. That is the 28th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai for Thirukkadavur Veerattanam, set to the tune of Nattaraga Pann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Podiyar meniyanai purinool orupal poruntha vadiyar moovilai mel valar angaiyin mangaiyodum kadiyar konraiyane kadavur thanul veerattaththu em adikel en amuthe enakku arthunai nee allathe." "Kararum pozhilsoozh kadavur thiruveerattaththul erarum iraiyai thunaiya ezhil navalar kon arooran adiyan adiththondan uraiththa thamil paror eththavallar paralogaththu iruppare." Thiruchitrambalam. We have already contemplated the temple histories of Thirukkadavur and Thirukkadavur Mayanam in the Puranams of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman and Thirugnanasambandha Peruman. Having worshipped thus, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal proceeded to Thiruvazhamburam.

The 147th verse: "He worshipped the feet of the Lord of Thiruvazhamburam, with its mountain-like ramparts, and sang a Thiruppathigam beginning with 'Enakku Ini'. Then he reached Thiruchaikkadu, where the ocean worships with conches, fragrant incense, jewel lamps, pearl flowers, and waves." This is the 147th verse. He worshipped the feet of the Lord enshrined in Thiruvazhamburam, with its mountain-like ramparts, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal sang a Thiruppathigam beginning with 'Enakku Ini', where words and meaning align. This Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal for Thiruvazhamburam is the 72nd Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Gandharam Pann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Enakku ini thinaiththanai pugazh idam arinthen panaikkani pazhampadum paravaiyin karaimel enakku iniyavan thamarkku iniyavan ezhumaiyum manakku iniyavan thanathu idam valamburame." "Varum kalamum pala penuthal karungadal irungula pirappartham idam valamburathinai arungulaththu arunthamizhuran vanthondan sol perungulaththavaru pithatruthal perumaiye." Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruvazhamburam is the 44th shrine on the southern bank of the Kaveri River. We have contemplated the history of this shrine in the Puranam of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman. Having worshipped Thiruvazhamburam, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal proceeded to Thiruchaikkadu. It is a place located on the seashore, where the ocean worships with musical instruments, offering foam and spray as incense, precious gems as lamps, pearls as flowers, and waves as hands. This shrine, called Thiruchaikkadu or Sayavanam, is praised as being equal to Kasi. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal arrived there. He sang and worshipped the Lord there. However, the Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal for Thiruchaikkadu is not available to us, due to our lack of merit.

The 148th verse: "Having worshipped the Lord in Thiruchaikkadu, and sung a garland of beautiful Tamil verses, the poet-king then worshipped Thiruvengadu, where the Lord burnt the three cities of the enemies, and reached the city of Thirunanippalli." Having worshipped the Lord in Thiruchaikkadu and sung a garland of beautiful Tamil verses, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal proceeded further and worshipped Thiruvengadu, where the Lord burnt the three cities of the enemies. The Thiruppathigam sung by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal for Thiruvengadu is the 6th Thiruppathigam in the 7th Thirumurai, set to the tune of Indalappann. The first and last verses of this Thiruppathigam are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Padankol nagam senni serththi paypuliththol araiyil veekki adangalor oor eriya seeri andru moovarkku arul purintheer madangal anai setru ugandheer manaikalthorum thalai kaiyenthi vidangaragi thirivathiyanne velai soozh venkada neere." "Viriththa vedam othavallar velai soozh venkadu meya viruththanaya vedhan thannai viri pozhil thirunavaluran aruththiyal arooran thondan adiyanketta malai paththum theriththavannam mozhiyavallar semmaiyalar vanvulare." Thiruchitrambalam.

Having worshipped Thiruvengadu, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal received the Lord's grace and proceeded to the city of Thirunanippalli. Let us continue our contemplation. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Periya Puranam, Part 861, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkaama Nayanar Puranam. The 149th verse.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 861, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkaama Nayanar Puranam. The 149th verse. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, having prostrated at the feet of the Lord residing in Thirunanipalli, and having offered a pure and fragrant garland of good Tamil verses, proceeds to worship at Thirusembanpalli and many other abodes of the Lord with the moon-adorned matted locks, before arriving at Thirunintriyur on his singular bull mount. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prostrates at the feet of the Lord who lovingly resides in Thirunanipalli and offers a sweet, pure, and fragrant garland of Tamil verses, which is a *Thiruppathigam* (a devotional hymn). This *Thiruppathigam* is praised by Sekkizhar Peruman as "Narsamizhin Punitha Narumthodai" (a pure and fragrant garland of good Tamil). The qualities of goodness, sweetness, purity, and fragrance are the special features of this *Thiruppathigam*. These can be individually observed in this *Thiruppathigam*.

The *Thiruppathigam* offered by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal to Thirunanipalli is the 97th *Thiruppathigam* in the 7th *Thirumurai* (collection of hymns), set to the *Panchamam* *pann* (melody). The first and last verses of this *Thiruppathigam* are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Adhiyan Adhiraiyan Ayan Maal Aridarku Ariya Sodhiyan Sol Porulaya Surungaa Marai Naankinaiyum Odhiyan Umbardham Kon Ulakathinul Evvuyirkkum Naadhiyan Namberuman Nannum Oor Nanipalli Adhe." "Kaalamum Naazhigaiyum Nanipalli Manathin Kolamadhayavanai Madhithu Uraippaar Mann Marandhu Vaanor Ulakil Saala Nallam Eythi Thavalogathu Iruppaare." Thiruchitrambalam. In the 9th verse of this *Thiruppathigam*, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises Thirugnanasambandha Peruman. "Ena Maruppinadum Ezhil Aamaiyum Poondhu Ukandhu Vaanmadhil Aranam Malaiye Silaiya Valaitthaan Oonamil Kaali Thannul Uyar Gnanasambandharku Andru Gnanam Arul Purindhaan Nannum Oor Nanipalli Adhe." In this 9th verse, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises, "Oonamil Kaali Thannul Uyar Gnanasambandharku Andru Gnanam Arul Purindhaan" (He who bestowed knowledge upon the exalted Gnanasambandhar in the flawless Kali age). Having thus praised Thirunanipalli, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal proceeds to Thirusembanpalli and worships the Lord. From Thirusembanpalli, he sets out and visits Thiruvariyalur, Thiruvizhanagar, Thirumayiladuthurai, Thirukancharu, and other holy places, finally arriving at Thirunintriyur. The 450th verse. Sekkizhar Peruman composes this verse, saying, "Nintriyur Meyaarai Neyathal Pukku Irainghi Ondri Anbu Ulluruga Paadiye Ulagu Idar Neenga Paadiya Ezhu Ezhunoorum Andru Sirappithu Ansol Thiruppathigam Arul Seidhaar." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises the Lord residing in Thirunintriyur with a *Thiruppathigam*. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, with a heart full of melting love, sings in this *Thiruppathigam*, mentioning the number of *Thiruppathigams* composed by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, thereby praising Thirunavukkarasu Peruman and composing a verse in this *Thiruppathigam*. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal states that Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, the "Aludaiya Arasugal" (the ruling king), sang 7,700 *Thiruppathigams* for the world to be free from suffering and attain happiness. Sekkizhar Peruman thus illustrates the greatness of this *Thiruppathigam* where Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman always sang for the world to be free from suffering. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman composed *Thiruppathigams* for the world to be eternally free from suffering and to prosper. In the history of the Lord's life, we see how the world was freed from various sufferings on the day Thirunavukkarasu Peruman sang *Thiruppathigams*. Not only on that day, but just as it was then, the "Arasugal" (king) sang for the world to be eternally free from suffering and to prosper. During the time of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman's incarnation, the *Thiruppathigams* brought about the removal of worldly suffering, such as the healing of the son of Appoodhi Adigal from snake venom, the alleviation of famine by receiving *Padikkasu* (coins) at Thiruvizhimizhalai, the opening of the temple doors at Thirumaraikkadu, and the removal of the obstruction by Jains at Thirupazhaiyarai Vaduthazhi, transforming it into a *Vimanam* (temple tower) for the Lord. We have seen all these miraculous deeds in his sacred history. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal states that Thirunavukkarasu Swamigal sang a total of 7,700 *Thiruppathigams*. Therefore, 7,700 *Thiruppathigams* amount to 4,900 *Thiruppathigams*. Nambiandar Nambigal, in his 11th *Thirumurai*, in the work called "Thirunavukkarasar Thiru Ekadasamalai," praises Thirunavukkarasu Peruman as "Pathigam Ezhu Ezhunooru Pagarum Maa Kavi Yogi" (the great poet who sang 7,700 *Thiruppathigams*). In the second verse of the Thirunintriyur *Thiruppathigam*, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal sings, "Ezhu Ezhunooru Iru Panuval Indranaavinuku Araiyan" (the king of tongues who gave 7,700 works). The first verse of such a Thirunintriyur *Thiruppathigam*, and the second and sixth verses that mention the number of *Thiruppathigams* sung by Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, are as follows: The Thirunintriyur *Thiruppathigam* is the 65th *Thiruppathigam* in the 7th *Thirumurai*, set to the *Thakkesi* *pann*. Thiruchitrambalam. "Thiruvum Vanmaiyum Thinthiral Arasum Silandhiyar Seidha Seyini Kandu Maruvu Kosengannan Thanaku Aliththa Vaarthai Kettu Nunmalar Adi Adaindhen Perugu Ponni Vandhu Undhu Panmaniyai Pillai Palganam Pannaiyul Nanni Theruvum Thettriyum Mutramum Patri Thirattum Then Thirunintriyurane." "Anigol Aadai Hamboona Animaalai Amudhu Seidhu Amudhamperu Thandi Inaikkol Ezhu Ezhunooru Irum Panuval Eendra Naavinuku Araiyan Kanaikkol Kannappan Endru Ivar Petra Kaadhal In Arul Aadharithu Adaindhen Thinaikkul Senthamizh Paingizhi Theriyaum Selvam Then Thirunintriyurane." "Kaadhu Potharai Kinnarar Ozhuvai Kadikkum Pannagam Pidipparum Sim Kothin Maadhavar Kuzhuvudan Ketpa Kolavaanizhal Keel Aram Pagara Edham Seidhavar Eythiya Inbam Yaanum Kettu Nin Inaiyadi Adaindhen Needhi Vedhiyar Niraipugazh Ulakinil Nilavu Then Thirunintriyurane." Thiruchitrambalam. This *Thiruppathigam* was composed by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal with the intention that he too came here after hearing about the gracious deeds of Lord Shiva and praising them. In every verse, one or more historical accounts of Lord Shiva's gracious deeds are extensively elaborated upon. This entire *Thiruppathigam* is a very rare *Thiruppathigam* and is worthy of recitation. The last three verses of this *Thiruppathigam* are not available to us. Thirunintriyur is the 19th *Thalam* (sacred place) on the northern bank of the Cauvery. We have already contemplated this sacred history in Appar Peruman's Puranam. Thus, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal offers the *Thiruppathigam*. Now, the 151st verse. "Appathiyil Anbarudan Amarndhu Agazhvaar Igalidathil Seppariya Pugazh Needur Paniyadha Selpozhudhil Oppariya Unarvinaal Ninaithu Aruli Thozhil Uruvaar Mei Porul Van Tamil Maalai Vilambiye Meendu Anaindhaar." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, having lovingly resided with the devotees in Thirunintriyur, continues his sacred journey. At that time, as he proceeded on his journey without worshipping at Thiruneedur, a place of indescribable fame, he remembered Thiruneedur with unparalleled true awareness. Therefore, to worship Thiruneedur, he returns here and offers a garland of Tamil verses, a *Thiruppathigam*, to Thiruneedur. When he was leaving Thirunintriyur and started to proceed further without visiting the nearby Thiruneedur, an unparalleled true awareness reminded Sundaramoorthy Swamigal about Thiruneedur. This arises from a state of never forgetting Shiva. It is a rule that if there is a Shiva temple on the way, devotees must visit and worship there before proceeding further. To bypass this rule is a mistake, and true awareness itself reveals this. That is the characteristic of true awareness. The rich *Thiruppathigam* that emerged about such a true essence is the *Thiruppathigam* offered by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal to Thiruneedur. Sekkizhar Peruman explains Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's offering of the *Thiruppathigam* to Thiruneedur in the 152nd verse. "Madalaarum Punal Needur Maruvinar Thazh Vanangaadhu Vidaalaame Enum Kaadhal Viruppurum Aththiruppathigam Adaalaaru Suzhappadaiyaar Tham Paadi Adivanangi Udalaaru Mayirp Pulagam Nigappaninndhu Amaigindradhu." This verse states that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises the Lord of Thiruneedur with that *Thiruppathigam*, which expresses the desire, "Can one leave without worshipping the feet of the Lord who lovingly resides in Thiruneedur, a place rich in water with abundant flowers?" He sings about the powerful Lord with the discus weapon, prostrates at His feet, and with his entire body covered in goosebumps, he remains in that sacred place. The *Thiruppathigam* offered by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal to Thiruneedur is the 56th *Thiruppathigam* in the 7th *Thirumurai*, set to the *Thakkesi* *pann*. The first and last verses of this *Thiruppathigam* are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Oorvadhu Or Vidai Ondru Udaiyaanai On Nudhal Thani Kan Nudhalaanai Kaaradhaar Karai Maadattraanai Karudhalaar Puram Moondru Eriththaanai Neeril Vaazhai Varaal Kudhikollum Nirai Punal Kazhani Selvam Needur Paarvulaar Paravi Thozhanindra Paramani Paniyadha Vidaalaame." "Peror Aayiramum Udaiyaanai Pesinaal Peridhum Iniyaanai Neerur Vaarsadai Ninmalan Thannai Needur Nindru Ukandha Piranaai Aaruran Adi Kaanbadharku Anbaai Aadharithu Azhaithitta Immaalaai Paarurum Paravi Thozhavallaar Pattharaai Mutthidhaam Peruvaare." Thiruchitrambalam. The Lord of Thiruneedur is Arulsomanatheswarar, Nirthagana Priyar, Gana Nira Sankarar, Bhadrakaleeswarar. The Goddess is Adithya Abhaya Prathambikai, Vedanayaki, Aalala Sundaranayaki, Veyuru Thozhiyamai. We have contemplated the history of Thiruneedur in Thirunavukkarasu Peruman's Puranam. Now, the 153rd and 154th verses. "Angan Inidhu Amarndhu Arulaal Thiru Punkur Anaindhu Irainghi Kongalarum Malarcholai Thiru Kolakka Anaiya Gangai Sadai Karandhavar Thaam Edhirkaatchi Koduttharula Pongu Viruppaal Thozhudhu Thiruppathigam Potrisaippaar Thirugnanasambandhar Thirukkaigalal Otri Perugu Aarvathudan Paada Pingyanar Kandu Irainghi Arulaale Thirutthaalam Aliththapadi Sirappithu Porul Maalai Thiruppathigam Paadiye Potriseidhaar Enbavai Thiruppaadalkal." These verses state that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, after worshipping at Thiruneedur and receiving the Lord's grace, proceeds to Thirupunkur and worships the Lord there. He then arrives at Thirukolakka, a place surrounded by fragrant flower gardens. At that time, the Lord, who concealed the Ganga in His matted locks, appeared before Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. With overflowing devotion, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prostrated and sang a *Thiruppathigam* in praise. He also praised the Lord who, seeing Thirugnanasambandhar sing with great enthusiasm, beating time with his hands, graciously bestowed golden cymbals upon him, and sang a *Thiruppathigam* as a garland of true meaning. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, after worshipping at Thiruneedur and receiving the Lord's grace, proceeds to Thirupunkur and worships the Lord. Then, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal arrives at Thirukolakka, which is surrounded by beautiful groves. At that time, the Lord appears before Sundaramoorthy Swamigal outside the town. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises the Lord who appeared before him even before he entered the temple at Thirukolakka, and offers a *Thiruppathigam*. The refrain "Kolakkavinil Kandukondene" (I saw Him in Kolakka) appears in every verse of this *Thiruppathigam* dedicated to Thirukolakka. The *Thiruppathigam* offered by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal to Thirukolakka is the 62nd *Thiruppathigam* in the 7th *Thirumurai*, set to the *Thakkesi* *pann*. The first, fifth, eighth, and tenth verses of this *Thiruppathigam* are as follows: Thiruchitrambalam. "Putril Vaazh Aravu Aarthapiranaai Bhoothanaadhanai Paadhame Thozhuvaar Patruvaan Thunai Enaku Elivandha Paavanaasanai Mevariyaanai Muttralaar Thirupuram Oru Moondrum Pondra Vendri Maal Varai Ari Ambaa Kotravil Angai Endhiya Konai Kolakkavinil Kandukondene." "Andru Vandhu Ennai Agalidaththavar Munnaaladhaaga Endru Aavanam Kaatti Nindru Vennai Nallurmisai Ozhiththa Nitthila Thiral Thotthinai Mutthiku Ondrinaan Thanaai Umbar Piranaai Uyarum Val Aranam Keda Seerum Kundravilliyai Melliyaludanai Kolakkavinil Kandukondene." "Naalum Innisaiyaal Thamizh Parappum Gnanasambandhanuku Ulakavar Mun Thaalam Eendhu Avan Paadaluku Iraingum Thanmaiyaalanai En Manakkaruthai Aalum Bhoothangal Paada Nindru Aadum Angananthanai En Ganam Iraingum Kozhili Perungoyil Ullaanai Kolakkavinil Kandukondene." "Kodaramabaiyil Sadaivudai Karumbai Kolakkavul Emmanai Meimmanai Paadar Angudi Adiyavar Virumba Payilum Naaval Aaruran Van Thundan Naadu Irainghi Mun Ariyum Anneriyaal Navindra Pathu Ivai Vilambiya Maandhar Kaadu Arangu Ena Nadam Navindraanpaal Gathiyum Eythuvar Padhi Avarku Adhuve." Thiruchitrambalam. Thirukolakka is the place where the Lord bestowed cymbals upon Thirugnanasambandha Peruman. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal praises and sings this *Thiruppathigam*, a garland of true meaning, extolling the Lord's gracious act of bestowing golden cymbals upon Thirugnanasambandhar, who sang with great enthusiasm, beating time with his hands. The verse that narrates this sacred history is the eighth verse in this *Thiruppathigam*, which begins with "Naalum Innisaiyaal Thamizh Parappum Gnanasambandhanuku." Now, the 155th verse. "Moovaadha Muzhu Mudalaaru Mudhal Kolakka Agandru Thaavaadha Pugazh Sanbai Valam Kondu Thaazhndhu Irainghi Naavaar Mutthamizh Viragar Narpadhangal Paravippoy Mevardham Puram Setraar Kurugaavur Mevuvaar." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, having received the Lord's grace from Thirukolakka, circumambulates Sanbai, also known as Sirkazhi, a place of undying fame, prostrates, praises the sacred feet of Thirugnanasambandha Nayanar, the master of the three forms of Tamil, and then proceeds to Thirukurugavur, where Lord Shiva resides. We will continue to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 862, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkaama Nayanar Puranam. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, departing from Thirukolakka, arrives near Sirkazhi and circumambulates the sacred place of Sirkazhi without entering it. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal circumambulates the sacred place of Sirkazhi and worships it, fearing to step inside the *Thalam* (sacred place) of Sirkazhi. We contemplated in the *Thaduthatkonda Puranam* (the Puranam of being stopped and taken over) that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, not wanting to step inside the great and famous sacred place where Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, the *Aludaiya Pillaiyar* (the Lord's child), incarnated, worshipped from the outskirts, and the Lord appeared before him. Similarly, now, because it is the birthplace of the *Pillaiyar* (child), he does not step inside but circumambulates the town from outside, praises the feet of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman, and proceeds further. Thus, he goes and arrives at Thirukurugavur. There, the Lord prepares *Podhisoru* (packed food) and water for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and his companions, and offers it to them, quenching their thirst and hunger. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing about this miraculous event. The verse: "Vetkai Pasiyaal Mozhi Paravaiyar Varum Paangar Needu Thirunudhalla Kaadhal Vara Karuthu Arindhu Thanneerum Podhisorum Kondu Vazhi Saargindrar." This verse states that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, the husband of Paravai Nachiyar, who has a sweet voice, approaches. Paravai Nachiyar is known for her sweet voice, which is characteristic of high-born women. Her speech naturally carries the quality of a *pann* (melody). Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, her husband, approaches Thirukurugavur with his companions. The Lord realizes that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is suffering greatly from thirst and hunger. *Neervetkai* means thirst. *Unneerin Vetkai* means the desire for drinking water, which needs to be precisely prepared and consumed. Water, besides being a cause for preparing other food items, also has the special quality of being a food item itself. Thus, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal approaches, suffering from thirst and hunger. Great souls sometimes experience hunger and thirst. It does not always appear in great souls; it appears occasionally. But in others, like us ordinary people, eating is always the profession. That situation does not exist for great souls. Even if hunger and thirst afflict them, great souls do not acknowledge them or give them importance, but continue in their devotion to Shiva. Previously, we saw a similar sacred history when Thirunavukkarasu Peruman was approaching Thirupangeli. Here, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal stands in Shiva's service, disregarding his bodily discomfort. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal did not acknowledge the suffering of hunger and thirst, but stood in Shiva's service. However, the Lord, who is the life of his life, residing within his thoughts, knows all these things. He waits with water and *Podhisoru*. There, just as the *Sivagnana Bodham* (a philosophical text) states, "Kandu Kaattalin" (by showing), in its 11th *Sutra* (aphorism), that the Primeval Being directly experiences what is perceived by souls, and just as it is quoted that "He also experiences their (the souls') matters," the Lord, who is the life of Nambigal's life, knows Nambigal's thirst and hunger. He is *Kannidu Thirunudhalaar* (one with a long, graceful forehead), one whose gracious gaze extends far. Therefore, He prepares water and *Podhisoru* and waits on the path where Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is coming. *Podhisoru* means packed rice. It is rice packed with curries and other food items. It is called *Kattusoru* (tied rice). Thirst is more severe than hunger. Therefore, water is placed first, and hunger second, and accordingly, the verse is arranged as "Thanneerum Podhisorum" (water and packed food). The Lord, assuming a sacred disguise, waits on the path where Nambigal is coming. Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, in his sacred words, has defined the duties of the Lord and the servant as "Than Kadan Adiyenaiyum Thaangudhal En Kadan Pani Seidhu Kidappadhe" (His duty is to support me, my duty is to serve and remain). Here, we see the Lord's duty placed first. The 157th verse. "Venil Oru Veyil Vemmai Thanipadharku Virai Kulir Menpaan Nal Malarthadambolum Pandhar Orupal Amaithe Aan Marai Vedhiyarai Arulvedam Kondirundhar Maanumarum Thirukkaraththaar Vandondar Thamai Paarthu." It is summer, and there is the heat of the sun. To alleviate the heat, the Lord, holding a deer in His sacred hand, assumes the sacred disguise of a Vedic Brahmin, and sets up a *pandhal* (temporary shelter) like a fragrant, cool, soft lotus pond on one side, anticipating the arrival of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. It is summer, so there is the heat of the sun. To alleviate the heat of walking in the sun and the heat that would arise at the time of resting and eating the *Podhisoru* here, He sets up a cool *pandhal* like a lotus pond or a flower garden. He sets up this *pandhal* by the side of the path where Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is coming, and He, the Lord, assumes the sacred disguise of a Vedic Brahmin and waits there. It is a disguise of grace. The Lord has assumed this disguise to manifest His compassion. This disguise assumed by the Lord is not an illusory form like the disguises of others; it is a sacred form taken as the embodiment of compassion itself. He waits, anticipating Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's arrival. The Lord's action precedes the devotee's action. Just as it is said, "Avan Arulaale Avan Thazh Vanangi" (by His grace, worshipping His feet) and "Aattuviththaal Aaroruvar Aadaadhaare" (who can dance if not made to dance), among the two actions, the action of the soul and the grace of the Lord, the Lord's gracious action occurs first and precedes. Why does the Lord wait for Sundaramoorthy Swamigal? Because Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is a *Van Thondar* (a strong devotee). He is the one whom the Lord graciously accepted as His servant, even though he spoke strongly against the Lord, and the Lord Himself came and took him over. Therefore, it is the duty of the leader to prevent suffering rather than to alleviate the suffering of those who have accepted him as their leader. Just as Sundaramoorthy Swamigal says, "Vanmaigal Pesida Van Thondan Enbadhor Vaazhvu Thandhaar" (He gave me a life as a strong devotee for speaking strongly), and just as Thirunavukkarasu Peruman says, "Theerppadhandro Thalaiyaayavar Kadanavadhu Thaan" (Is it not the duty of the foremost to alleviate suffering?), the Lord thus assumes a sacred disguise and waits to quench Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's thirst and hunger. The 158th verse. "Kurugaavur Amarndharulum Kuzhagar Vazhi Paarthiruppa Thiruvur Thambiraan Thozhar Thiruththondarudan Varuvaar Appandhar Idai Pugundhu Thirumaraiyavar Paal Perugu Aarvam Selaiyirundhaar Sivaayanama Ena Pesi." The Lord, who lovingly resides in Thirukurugavur, the *Kuzhagar* (the youthful one), as mentioned earlier, was watching for the arrival of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, the *Van Thondar*. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, the friend of the Lord from Thiruvur, would come with his devotees. When he came, he entered the *pandhal* set up by the Lord on the path. There, he approached the Lord, who was seated in the sacred disguise of a Vedic Brahmin, with great enthusiasm, and saying "Sivaya Nama," he sat down. The *pandhal* set up by the Lord was such that those who passed by could not avoid entering it. It was arranged in such a way, by its form, grace, and location, that those who came that way could not but enter that *pandhal*. Just as Appoodhi Nayanar set up a water *pandhal*, and Thirunavukkarasu Peruman, who came that way, entered it, similarly here, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, with his devotees, enters the *pandhal* and sits near the Lord, who is in the disguise of a Brahmin, saying "Sivaya Nama." It is a tradition for great souls, when they meet, to first praise the Lord's name and then begin to speak. This tradition, which Sundaramoorthy Swamigal follows here, unknowingly becomes a praise to the Lord standing before him, and we see it bearing fruit. Therefore, we realize here that all the traditions established by great souls are traditions related to such benefits. Now, the 159th, 160th, and 161st verses. "Aazha Nizhal Keel Irundhaar Avar Thammai Edhirnokki Saala Miga Pasiththeer Ippodhisoru Tharugindren Kaalamini Thaazhaame Kai Kondu Inidhu Arundhi Ela Narum Kulirthanneer Kudithu Izhaipu Theerum Ena Vanthondar Adhu Kettu Marai Munivar Tharum Podhisoru Indru Namaku Edhir Vilakkalaagadhu Endru Isaindharuli Pondhayangu Noolmaarbhar Tharum Podhisoru Adhu Vaangi Sendra Thiruththondarudan Thiruvamudhu Seidharuli Enniraaindha Parisanangal Ellaarum Inidhu Arundha Panniyapin Ammarungu Pasithu Anaindhaargalum Arundha Un Niraindha Aaramudhaai Oru Kaalam Ulavadhe Punniyanaartham Aliththa Podhisoru Pozhindhadha." These three verses describe the event. The Lord, who is seated under the shade of a banyan tree, here sits under the *pandhal*. The Lord, thus seated, addresses Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, saying, "You are very hungry. I will give you this *Podhisoru* that I have. Do not delay any longer. Take it and eat it sweetly, drink this good cool water, and relieve your weariness." The Vedic Brahmin says, "I will give you this *Podhisoru*." The meaning of this is, "I am an *Anaadhi Saivan* (an eternal devotee of Shiva). You are an *Aadhisaivar* (a Brahmin priest of Shiva) who will come by our grace. By this comparison, the food I give is acceptable." Therefore, now, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal also decides that he should accept the *Podhisoru* given by this Brahmin, as the Brahmin said. The Vedic Brahmin says, "Do not delay any longer." It is a compassionate word, expressing concern that if he delays any longer, hunger and the suffering that comes with it will increase even more. There is cool water suitable for that *Podhisoru* meal. Medical science states that cool water is suitable for drinking. Medical science states that only those with illness should consume hot water. Therefore, here, there is cool water suitable for the *Podhisoru*. The Lord says, "Eat the sacred food so that your hunger, thirst, heat from the sun, and fatigue from walking on the path are all relieved." The *Van Thondar* (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal), hearing this, thinks that he should accept this *Podhisoru* given by this Vedic Brahmin, and it is not proper for him to refuse it. He agrees to it. Although it is a tradition for great souls to refuse food offered by strangers on the way for some reason, here, this tradition cannot be applied. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal decides that he cannot refuse the words of the Brahmin. Therefore, by the Lord's gracious gaze and words, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal accepts the *Podhisoru* given by the Lord, who has a chest adorned with a golden sacred thread, and partakes of the sacred food with the devotees who came with him. After all the countless companions have eaten sweetly, those who arrived hungry in that vicinity also eat there. The *Podhisoru* flowed like abundant sweet nectar, never diminishing in any way, given by the virtuous Vedic Brahmin with compassion. Even though the Lord was seated there to give *Podhisoru* and water to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and his accompanying devotees, those who passed by on the way also came to that *pandhal* and accepted the *Podhisoru* and water. Therefore, the Lord, who preached *Dharma* (righteousness), here demonstrates that these acts of charity are also to be performed. This charity of giving water and food to Nambigal and his companions is a *Pathi Dharma* (duty to the Lord). When it was given to others who came hungry, it became a *Pasu Dharma* (duty to living beings). Since the Lord Himself performed these *Dharmas*, their benefits reached those who accepted this food and water. If the *Podhisoru* and water given by the Lord were one and the same, then all those who ate it, except Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, were not as pure and exalted as Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Therefore, here we see the Lord's grace bestowed according to the level of maturity of the souls. Like an inexhaustible treasure, that abundant nectar, the *Podhisoru*, and the cool water were consumed by everyone, quenching their thirst and hunger. It was food and water graciously given by the Lord. The Lord gave it to Nambigal, His devotee, who was suffering greatly from thirst and hunger. It also benefited the other companions and those who came there. Therefore, the *Podhisoru* and water that the Lord had prepared for Nambigal also benefited others. In this world, although it is truly the Lord who creates water and food and helps all beings to alleviate hunger, here, the Lord Himself made all those food items into *Podhisoru*, and it was consumed by Nambigal and all those who came as travelers, by their fate and destiny. Now, the 162nd verse. "Sankaranar Thiru Arul Pol Thanneerin Suvai Aarnthu Pongivarum Aadharavaal Avar Naamam Pugazhndhu Ethi Angu Ayarvaal Amarndhu Arugu Anaindhaargalum Thuyila Gangai Sadai Karandhaar Appandharodum Thaam Karandhaar." Just like the grace of Sankaranar, the water was also sweet, and with overflowing love, they praised His name. There, Nambigal, due to fatigue, lay down and slept, and those who had approached nearby also slept. The Lord, who concealed the Ganga in His matted locks, disappeared along with the *pandhal*. Sankaranar means one who brings happiness. Here, the name is significant because He waited on the path, gave *Podhisoru* and water, and removed their fatigue, thus bringing happiness. Just as the Lord's grace is sweet, the water was also sweet. The food consumed was as sweet and pleasant as the Lord's grace. With ever-increasing love, Nambigal praised and glorified the Lord's sacred name, the *Thiru Aindhezhuthu* (the five-letter mantra). There, due to bodily fatigue, Nambigal lay down and slept. The Lord's name, the *Thiru Aindhezhuthu*, is sweet like the juice of sugarcane that has been crushed. This is a sacred saying from *Thevaram*. Earlier, when Sundaramoorthy Swamigal first met the Vedic Brahmin, we saw that he sat down saying "Sivaya Nama." Now, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, unknowingly, praises the name of that Shiva Brahmin. It is the nature of great souls to praise Lord Shiva, considering all good things, no matter who brings them, as Shiva's grace. "Vazhukki Veezhinum Thiruppeyarallaal Matra Naan Ariyen Marumaatram" (Even if I stumble and fall, I know no other word than Your sacred name) is a sacred saying from Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's *Thevaram*. "Naan Marakkinum Sollum Naan Amasivayave" (Even if I forget, my tongue will utter "Nama Sivaya") is also Nambigal's sacred saying. Thus, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, having consumed the food and water while contemplating the Lord's name, lies down there, overcome by the Lord's grace. In reality, it was not the time, period, or place for sleeping. However, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, overcome by the Lord's grace, sleeps thus. As Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and those who had come there slept, Lord Shiva, who concealed the Ganga in His matted locks, disappeared along with the *pandhal*. The 163rd verse. "Siththanilai Thiriyaadha Thirunaavaluur Mannar Atthagudhiyinil Palli Unarndhu Avarai Kaanaamal Itthanai Yaamatra Marandhilen Ena Eduthu Meiththagaiya Thiruppathigam Vilambiye Sendradaindhaar." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, the king of Thirunavalur, whose mental state never wavers, even while sleeping, remains in a state of *Sivayoga* (union with Shiva), never forgetting Shiva, with a conscious sleep. Even in such a state of *Sivayoga*, he cannot see the Lord unless the Lord reveals Himself. Therefore, while he was sleeping, after a short while, due to divine grace, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal wakes up from his sleep. At that time, he sees that the Vedic Brahmin and the cool *pandhal* have disappeared. He realizes this.
