In Sirkazhi, there is the sacred house where Thirugnanasambandha Peruman incarnated. All these are priceless treasures for the Shaivite community. Similarly, this sacred mansion where our Sangili Nachiyar incarnated should also shine in the same way. It should be protected as a sacred monastery where Shaivites worship. Protecting and worshipping these is a great duty of Shaivites. Sivakavimani Desikanar also prays that divine grace should facilitate this. In such a place called Gnayiru, the fourth lineage, the Vellalar lineage, is classified in ancient Tamil texts. The classified lineage is the Vellalar lineage.

Among the many people, from the Brahmins to the Vellalars, who lived as good citizens with excellent conduct in such a lineage, in the fourth lineage, the Vellalar lineage, in that place called Gnayiru, there lived a great person named Gnayiru Kizhavar, who excelled in the characteristics of the Vellalars. Kizhavar is a special traditional name for Vellalars. It is also pronounced as Kizhar. Kizhamai means right or ownership. Those who have ownership are called Vellalars, meaning owners of the land. Therefore, it is customary to call them Kizhavar or Kizhar. This is their traditional name. Since he was a prominent and important person in the sacred place of Thirugnayiru, he was called Gnayiru Kizhar after the name of the village. We see names like Sengundrur Kizhar, Kovur Kizhar, and Kundaiyur Kizhar. Similarly, in this village of Gnayiru, he was prominent and well-known to everyone, so he was called Gnayiru Kizhar.

His sacred daughter who incarnated was Sangili Nachiyar. She was formerly known as Aninditaiyar in Thirukkailayam. Now, she incarnates here as Sangili Nachiyar, the sacred daughter of Gnayiru Kizhar. The three continuous verses, 208, 209, and 210, are as follows: "She who came with unforgetting love for the lotus feet of the daughter of the mountain (Uma), and whose consciousness was elevated, was Sangiliyar, who knew herself. She played with other young girls with wavy, spear-like eyes, and passed through all the stages of childhood. Not only did she excel in the conduct of her noble lineage, but she also possessed divine qualities that astonished everyone on earth. As her beautiful breasts grew, causing her waist to ache, her father said to his wife: 'Our daughter's form and qualities are not merely those of ordinary mortals, but are of a higher, divine nature. There is nothing comparable to her. The time for her marriage is approaching.' His wife, who was like a creeper of chastity, replied, 'I accept what you say.'"

The daughter of the mountain king (Uma Ammaiyar) is one whose love for the lotus-like feet is unforgettable, and who is foremost in that discipline. Aninditai, in her previous state, served Uma Ammaiyar in Thirukkailayam. With that consciousness, the Goddess incarnates in this world. She incarnates with the sacred name Sangili Nachiyar. Such an incarnation with prior consciousness occurs only by the grace of Shiva. We will see this in the sacred Puranam of Kochchengat Chola Nayanar. Sangili Nachiyar, in her previous state as Aninditai Ammaiyar, incarnates here with an inner knowledge of her true nature, which was not revealed to her by anyone else. The parents named the incarnated Aninditaiyar as Sangiliyar. She grows up, playing games appropriate for her age with groups of young girls, and passes through all the stages of life. Sangili Nachiyar not only excels in the conduct of her lineage, which is appropriate for her incarnation, but also possesses divine qualities. Sangili Ammaiyar grows up in a way that astonishes everyone in the world.

Growing up with divine qualities means that while living in this world, one does not engage in worldly affairs, but rather cultivates actions and words related to the Lord. As she grows up in this manner, Sangili Ammaiyar reaches the age of marriage. Her parents are astonished by Sangili Ammaiyar's divine qualities. Sangili Ammaiyar's father tells Sangili Ammaiyar's mother, "Our daughter's form and qualities are not only those of ordinary people, but she is also endowed with superior divine qualities. It is time for her marriage. Therefore, our daughter is superior to the people of this world, so we must find a suitable groom and arrange her marriage."

Sangili Ammaiyar's mother, understanding this, says, "Arrange her marriage in a suitable place, befitting our family's welfare and Sangili Ammaiyar's qualities and good character." Sangili Ammaiyar's mother continues to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 870, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkaama Nayanar Puranam. Sangili Ammaiyar's father and mother were discussing finding a suitable groom for Sangili Ammaiyar, and Sangili Ammaiyar overheard them. However, her father and mother were unaware that Sangili Ammaiyar was listening to their conversation. Sangili Nachiyar, who happened to be nearby, overheard her mother and father talking. The 211th verse: "Sangiliyar, who heard her father and mother speaking, said, 'This proposal is not for me. My life belongs to one who is fully blessed by our Lord, Ishan.' Fearing what might happen if her parents went against this principle, her consciousness became confused, and she fainted, falling to the ground." Sangili Ammaiyar, who heard her mother and father discussing her marriage, told them, "This talk of marriage is not suitable for me. My life belongs entirely to one who is fully blessed by the Lord." Fearing that her parents might do something contrary to this principle, Sangili Ammaiyar's consciousness became confused, and she fainted, falling to the ground. The passage from Thiruvachagam, "We are your devotees, who have you as our Lord. We will serve your devotees. We will be companions to them. They will be our husbands. Our breasts will not embrace those who are not your lovers," comes to our mind, doesn't it?

Now, the 212th verse: "Her father and mother, who were standing nearby, panicked, lifted her with tenderness, and with anguished hearts, asked, 'What has happened to her?' They supported her, sprinkled cool, fragrant rosewater, and stroked her, saying, 'What has come upon you, O fair-browed one with a bow-like forehead?'" As Sangili Ammaiyar fainted, her father and mother, who were nearby, panicked and tenderly lifted her. With anguished and confused hearts, they held Sangili Ammaiyar, asking, "What has happened to her?" Her father and mother had spoken as mentioned earlier, and Sangiliyar had heard them standing nearby. Sangiliyar, upon hearing it, had spoken thus and fainted. Her mother and father had spoken without realizing that Sangili Ammaiyar was standing nearby. Upon hearing their words, Sangili Ammaiyar replied, and before her parents could recover from their sudden astonishment, Sangili Ammaiyar fell to the ground and fainted. Immediately, her mother and father panicked, tenderly lifted her, and held her in their arms, asking, "What has happened to her?" We see this sequence of events. They sprinkled cool rosewater on Sangili Ammaiyar's body and stroked her, and her fainting and exhaustion subsided. Sangili Ammaiyar's parents experienced various emotions such as panic, tenderness, and anguish. When a beloved person suddenly shows signs of distress, those who love them experience events such as panic, tenderness, and anguish.

Panic is a trembling of the entire body due to fear. Tenderness is compassion. Anguish is mental suffering. Having experienced all these emotions, the parents supported Sangili Ammaiyar, sprinkled water on her, and relieved her fainting. They then asked, "What has happened to you here?" When her parents asked, Sangili Ammaiyar expressed her thoughts. The 213th verse: "When her parents asked, she spoke without hesitation: 'What you have said today about me is not suitable for my nature. I belong to one who has been blessed by the Lord with the victorious bull. From now on, I will go to Thiruvottriyur and live by the grace of Shiva.'" When her parents, who had given birth to her, asked as mentioned earlier, Sangili Nachiyar spoke her mind without hiding it. Here, since she had to answer her mother and father about her beloved, Sangili Ammaiyar, leaving aside the natural shyness inherent in women, spoke to her parents about her beloved. Sangili Ammaiyar, with the shyness inherent in womanhood, would not normally speak much about her beloved. But here, Sangili Ammaiyar, setting aside her shyness a little, is about to speak about her beloved. This is because a calamity is about to occur that could change the very essence and purpose of her life. When such a calamity is imminent, the truth must be revealed. If it is not revealed, her purpose will be ruined. Fearing this, and also because those who are asking are her own mother and father, Sangili Nachiyar speaks her mind without hesitation. What she says is that marrying her to anyone else is not suitable for her nature. This verse does not say "marry," but "what you have said," meaning, "if you do as you have said, it will not be suitable for my nature," says Sangili Nachiyar.

Due to the natural shyness of a woman, she should not even speak the word "marriage" to another man. Based on the power of chastity, Sangili Ammaiyar says that doing as they said is not suitable for her nature. Therefore, she says, "I will not belong to anyone else as you have said. I am one who belongs to a person who has received the grace of the Lord, who is the embodiment of the Lord's grace. My rightful Lord has already been granted by the grace of Lord Shiva. Until that marriage takes place, I will now go to Thiruvottriyur and live by the grace of the Lord, and by the grace of the Lord, I will obtain the one who is rightfully mine," says Sangili Nachiyar to her parents. The 214th verse: "Hearing those words, her father and mother were filled with weariness, fear, and wonder. They kept her words hidden from others. A man, ignorant of the nature of one equal to her in their noble lineage, desired her and sent some people to propose marriage. They went and spoke. The parents of the maiden, hearing this, were bewildered." Hearing Sangili Ammaiyar's words, her father and mother were filled with weariness, fear, and wonder. Sangili Ammaiyar's mother and father kept all these words that Sangili Ammaiyar had spoken to her parents hidden from everyone else. They kept it hidden from the outside world without telling them that this was Sangili Nachiyar's nature. Because Sangili Ammaiyar said that marrying her to anyone else, as her mother and father had decided, was not suitable for her nature, and because she spoke of severing worldly ties, her parents felt weary. Because she said, "I belong only to one who has received the grace of the Lord," her father and mother, not knowing that truth, feared that all their previous discussions would become an offense against Shiva. And because Sangili Ammaiyar said, "From now on, I will go to Thiruvottriyur and live by Shiva's grace," her parents were also filled with wonder upon hearing it. So, weariness, fear, and wonder came upon them all at once. However, even if they explained these matters to the world, they would not understand. Therefore, Sangili Ammaiyar's parents kept it hidden from the world. Nevertheless, it was very difficult for them to separate from their daughter and leave her in Thiruvottriyur as Ammaiyar wished. They did not agree to it. In this situation, a man, unaware of these qualities and truths, desired Sangili Ammaiyar and sent some people to propose marriage. They came to Sangili Ammaiyar's father, Gnayiru Kizhar, and asked for Sangili Ammaiyar for him. Sangili Ammaiyar had not told anyone about her decision, so her decision was unknown to anyone. Therefore, even if we assume that a man, unaware of all this, sent his relatives to propose marriage for Ammaiyar, the news that Sangili Ammaiyar, as she grew up, was not only excellent in ordinary worldly qualities but also possessed abundant extraordinary divine qualities, was known to everyone. Therefore, even after hearing that, this man should not have sent a marriage proposal to Ammaiyar's parents. If a man sends such a proposal even after knowing Ammaiyar's divine qualities, it means he does not know Ammaiyar's nature, nor does he know his own nature. Therefore, he sends his relatives for marriage negotiations. They come to Gnayiru Kizhar and convey the message. The 215th verse: "Her father, hearing that, unable to reveal her true nature, sent them away with words that would cause no harm. Before they could reach their destination, the one who had sent them died, as if he had committed a sin there. Those who had gone with him also died upon their return. The parents of the maiden, hearing this, were bewildered." The relatives sent by that man to propose marriage arrive. But Sangili Ammaiyar's father, without openly telling the visitors all the events and circumstances that had occurred so far, spoke some comforting words to them, so that they would not be saddened and would not face any difficulties. He told them that they were not in a position to agree to this marriage. Thus, Sangili Ammaiyar's father sent them away. This is a worldly custom. It is a good practice in worldly life to conceal the truth to some extent and indirectly refuse, so that no harm comes to anyone. The visitors might have been relatives. Therefore, there was a possibility of quarrels and suffering among relatives. Therefore, their intention was to avoid harm and bring about good. "If it brings about blameless good, even falsehood is truth," says Thirukkural. Therefore, concealing the truth to some extent and avoiding the harms that would come from telling the truth as it is, is a good practice in this world. At that time, Adigal Nayanar said, "He will not help here now." Those were words he spoke out of love for the Lord and love for his Guru. Similarly, in worldly life, in the path of good living, this practice is very applicable in terms of social harmony. Therefore, Sangili Ammaiyar's father sent them away with words that would not offend them. Before those who had come could return to their place, the one who had sent them to propose marriage died. And upon their return, those who had gone with him also died. Hearing this, the parents of the maiden were bewildered. Sangiliyar possessed divine chastity. Anyone who tried to harm her would face the death penalty. Here, the one who sent people to propose marriage to Sangili Ammaiyar dies. Therefore, that event takes place as if he died as a result of his evil deed. Even if poison is consumed unknowingly, it will kill the one who consumes it. Therefore, even if he did not intend to harm her, that action resulted in harm to Ammaiyar. Similarly, those who went to propose marriage and returned also went to the abode of Yama. Agreeing to his command and going and speaking were also offenses. Here, because two great offenses occurred, an offense against Shiva and an offense against chastity, those souls were punished. Hearing all this, Sangili Ammaiyar's parents were bewildered. This happened as if the Lord had set a rule for the people of this world to know that no one who wishes to live well would speak inappropriate words about Sangili Ammaiyar. Therefore, Sangili Ammaiyar's parents came forward to fulfill the action that Sangili Ammaiyar had spoken of, the action of going to Thiruvottriyur and seeking the grace of the Lord. We will continue to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 871, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkaama Nayanar Puranam. The 216th verse: "As if by a divine decree, that no one who wishes to live would speak inappropriate words about the maiden Sangiliyar, this event occurred. Her parents, with sorrowful hearts and fear, explained Sangiliyar's divine nature to the elders of their village as it was, and agreed to her wish." This verse states that as if by a divine decree, that no one who wishes to live in this world would speak inappropriate words about the maiden Sangiliyar, this event occurred. Sangili Ammaiyar's parents explained Sangiliyar's divine nature to the elders in their village as it truly was. Those parents, with very sorrowful hearts and fear, agreed to Sangiliyar's wish. They agreed to Sangili Ammaiyar's desired action, which she had spoken of, to perform Shiva tapas (penance) in Thiruvottriyur. The 217th verse: "This maiden's actions are divine, and those who know it fear to speak otherwise. She knows no words other than the glory of the Lord she worships. These are her qualities. Therefore, we shall take her to Thiruvottriyur, to the Lord with the serpent-crested matted hair, as she has desired." Sangili Ammaiyar is divine, a goddess among women. Those who know this would fear to speak any other words about Sangili Ammaiyar. Her parents clearly understood that Sangili Ammaiyar knew no words other than the glory of the Lord she worshipped. Sangili Ammaiyar's action was an action dedicated to Lord Shiva, and her parents and relatives clearly understood this. Therefore, Sangili Ammaiyar's parents decided that they should take Sangili Ammaiyar to the Lord in Thiruvottriyur, the Lord who has a hooded serpent on his matted hair. That was the best decision. Verses 218 and 219: "Her father and relatives, addressing Sangiliyar of sweet speech, said, 'Go to Thiruvottriyur, where the southern waters meet, and by the grace of the Lord with the eye on his forehead, reside in a Kanni Madam (maiden's hermitage) in that city surrounded by beautiful ponds, and perform penance.' Her father and relatives, knowing no other course of action by the will of the Lord with the crescent moon on his head, decided to do as the maiden Sangiliyar had said. With abundant wealth, they took her to Thiruvottriyur, to the Lord with the bow that destroys external forces." Her parents, relatives, and others gathered and spoke to Sangiliyar, who had sweet speech. "Ammaiyar, you should go to the city of Thiruvottriyur, where Lord Shiva resides, and worship the Lord there by His grace. You should reside there as you wish. We will arrange a Kanni Madam and provide facilities for you to perform penance," they said. Sekkizhar Peruman structures these lines in this verse as if her parents and others are speaking: "Go to Thiruvottriyur, and by the grace of the Lord with the eye on his forehead, reside in a Kanni Madam in that city surrounded by beautiful ponds, and perform penance." Selkathi means the ultimate goal to be attained, which is Mukti (liberation). Mukti, or liberation, is the ultimate and complete state that souls can attain. Sekkizhar Peruman has also used the word "gathi" (state) here. This also refers to Sangili Ammaiyar attaining Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, her groom, in Thiruvottriyur. Therefore, it is structured as "selkathi and by grace." Just as Sangili Ammaiyar said, "I belong to one who has been blessed by the Lord," here, the attainment of a beloved is mentioned. In accordance with her statement that she belongs to one who is filled with the grace of Lord Shiva, she is about to meet Sundaramoorthy Swamigal in Thiruvottriyur and attain that state by the grace of the same Lord. She is also about to attain the state of liberation in the future. Therefore, Sekkizhar Peruman structures it as if her parents and others are saying, "You will attain selkathi and by grace, reside there and perform penance." The Lord alone grants both worldly and ultimate benefits. Therefore, the philosophical meaning of their words is, "Perform penance and attain worldly benefits, and finally, liberation." Therefore, as her parents and relatives had said, by the grace of Lord Shiva, the Lord of Thiruvottriyur, they decided to do as Sangili Ammaiyar, the good woman, had said. With great wealth, they took Sangili Ammaiyar to Thiruvottriyur. Verses 220 and 221: "Entering the temple of Shiva, who wears the crescent moon on his head, they worshipped with their close relatives. With the consent of the elders of the ancient city, they established a Kanni Madam nearby, performed the necessary protective rituals, and arranged abundant wealth. Her father, bowing at her feet, said, 'We will serve you. You reside in this exalted Kanni Madam, desiring to serve the Lord.' As he spoke, tears flowed from his eyes, and he, along with his grieving relatives, bowed and departed to their fortified city." In Thiruvottriyur, where Lord Shiva resides, Sangili Ammaiyar, her parents, and relatives entered the temple and worshipped the Lord. Their village was Gnayiru, and now they had arrived at Thiruvottriyur. Therefore, to reside in the city of Thiruvottriyur, they sought the consent of the elders of that city. They sought the consent of the elders of Thiruvottriyur to establish a Kanni Madam near the Thiruvottriyur temple for Sangili Ammaiyar and her female companions to reside in. This is because they were from another village and were residing in another village. Therefore, they formally sought permission from the elders there. All those who were residing were women, so they also sought permission for security and made arrangements for it. Thus, Sangili Ammaiyar's parents did all these things formally. In those days, Thondai Nadu was divided into many sections such as Kottams, Nadus, Nattams, and Oors. Although these areas were under the imperial rule of Thondai Nadu, some of them also had independent administrative systems. In each village, there were village heads and village councils. These people, who were excellent in education, knowledge, and conduct in that village, were elected and appointed as village heads and council members, and they administered the village.

Those who were elected thus undertook the responsibility of providing village security and ensuring the well-being and security of the village. Such elders were called Nattamai or Oorar in those days. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to them here as Thollai Pathiyor (elders of the ancient city). The practice of electing them through elections also existed. We see this in the Uthiramerur inscription, ancient stone inscriptions, and ancient histories. We see that this practice existed in many parts of Tamil Nadu and Thondai Nadu until very recently. Today, we see that this system has completely disintegrated. Pathiyor refers to the village community that provided village security and the village council. Therefore, they were permanently settling Sangili Ammaiyar and her female companions in Thiruvottriyur from the village of Gnayiru. Therefore, they had to reside permanently from another village. In addition, they had to establish a Kanni Madam in a public place very close to the temple. Therefore, in this worldly context, they were in a position to seek the protection of the villagers. That is why Ammaiyar's parents formally obtained permission from the village elders to establish a Kanni Madam and reside there. They also established their own security in addition to public security. They settled female companions and maidservants in that Kanni Madam. Thus, after establishing the Kanni Madam, they also arranged the wealth necessary for Sangili Ammaiyar to perform her service to the Lord without any shortcomings. The wealth needed for Sangili Ammaiyar's life and the lives of her female companions, maidservants, etc., to be conducted properly, such as food items, clothing, etc., and items for Shiva tapas, these items were arranged as various types of wealth for obtaining them as goods, through barter, and by purchase, and given to Sangili Ammaiyar by her parents. After arranging all this, Sangili Ammaiyar's father came and bowed at Sangili Ammaiyar's feet. Here, can Sangili Ammaiyar's father bow at Sangili Ammaiyar's feet? Scriptures state that a father is one of the five gurus. Can a father, who is one of the gurus, bow at his daughter's feet? This question arises here. Although it is generally stated that way, in a special situation, one can bow. This is because Sangili Ammaiyar had said, "I belong to one who has been blessed by the Lord. From now on, I will go and live by Shiva's grace." Sangili Ammaiyar gives up all her connections to the one who has received the grace of Lord Shiva. Therefore, the relationship of father and daughter had already ceased to exist. From now on, Sangili Ammaiyar stands here as one who has taken a vow to perform Shiva's service, completely abandoning worldly life, saying that she belongs to a devotee who has received Shiva's grace. Therefore, bowing to such a person who has taken a vow is appropriate. That is why her parents, who until now spoke in the singular, "What has happened to her?", now speak in the plural, "to you." Thus, her father came and bowed at Sangili Ammaiyar's feet. Her father took leave of Ammaiyar. "We will perform all the services you need. You reside in this Kanni Madam to perform service suitable for the Lord," he said. Tears flowed uncontrollably from his eyes. "The relationship of father and daughter between us has now ceased. We will now be your servants, and you perform the Lord's service. Therefore, the only connection we now have is that of being your servants. The worldly attachment between us has ceased," he said. With sorrow and unbearable grief combined, tears flowed from his eyes. Unable to part from Sangili Ammaiyar, Ammaiyar's parents, along with their relatives, bowed and departed to their village, Gnayiru. Now, Sangili Ammaiyar performs Shiva tapas in the Kanni Madam in Thiruvottriyur. We will continue to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 872, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkaama Nayanar Puranam. Sangili Ammaiyar is performing penance in Thiruvottriyur. Sekkizhar Peruman continues to sing. The 222nd verse: "The maidens, who lovingly performed penance, resided there. They entered the temple of the Lord of all beings at all times, worshipped, and without deviating from the path of righteousness, performed the service assigned to them. They then went to a part of the flower pavilion, which was surrounded by screens, and sat there." Now, the 223rd verse: "With the understanding of the service performed in the sacred Kailash mountain in the past, the maiden, who was like a soft creeper of blooming flowers, with her mind fixed on it, prepared garlands of fragrant flowers, which bees frequented, to adorn the Lord of the celestials at appropriate times, and worshipped, and resided there." These two verses describe Sangili Ammaiyar, who resided in the Kanni Madam in Thiruvottriyur, lovingly and constantly meditating and performing penance as a maiden. The actions Sangili Ammaiyar performed during her stay in the Kanni Madam were of two types: those performed in the Kanni Madam and those performed in the temple. When residing in the Kanni Madam, Sangili Ammaiyar meditated on the Lord and performed penance. These included Shiva Puja, meditation, and so on. In the temple, Sangili Ammaiyar performed flower service. In addition, she went to the temple at all times of worship, from Thiruppalli Ezhuchi (waking the Lord) to Thiruppalli Arai (the Lord's chamber), worshipped, and performed flower service in the flower pavilion of the temple. At other times, she resided in the Kanni Madam and performed penance there. Without deviating from the prescribed method appropriate for her lineage, age, nature, and status, she performed the service assigned to her. The Agamas (scriptural texts) state that Shiva's services should be performed according to one's righteous path. Accordingly, she performed the service. The nature of the service Sangili Ammaiyar performed in Thirukailash in the past, those very feelings arose in Ammaiyar's sacred heart, and she performed the same service. In Thirukailash, Sangili Ammaiyar used to pluck flowers in the sacred garden and make garlands and other offerings. The same service, which she was inspired to do by divine grace in her sacred heart, she performed here as well. The continuation of that deep penance is also present here. The temple's pavilion is a flower pavilion. Freshly bloomed flowers are brought there. Devotees who are engaged in making garlands for the Lord perform that service there. Even today, we can see this directly in the flower pavilion in the Meenakshi Ammaiyar shrine in Thirualavai. The Agamas, such as Pushpa Vidhi, state that flowers appropriate for each time should be offered during the puja times, starting from dawn. This is stated in the Shivagamas. Accordingly, Sangili Ammaiyar performed the service. We have contemplated all these methods and Pushpa Vidhis mentioned in the Shivagamas when we read about the service performed by Sivakami Andar in the Thirupuranam of Eribattha Nayanar. We have also contemplated these in the Thirupuranam of Muruga Nayanar. Remembering all those details, we continue to contemplate this Puranam. Thus, Sangili Ammaiyar continued to perform her service. Now, the next verse, the 224th verse: "By the grace of the Lord with the evening hue, Arurar came. It was time for Sangiliyar, who made fragrant garlands, to be united in love. Therefore, by the ancient decree, which does not deviate from the ordained nature, one day, the Lord entered the temple." By the grace of the Lord, who has the hue of the evening, Nambi Arurar (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal) was born in Thirunavalur. By the grace of the Lord, he has now reached Thiruvottriyur. The time has now come for such a Nambi Arurar, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, to be united in love with Sangili Ammaiyar. This is by the ancient decree, which does not deviate from the ordained nature, as ordained by the Lord. The time has come for the marriage of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and Sangili Ammaiyar. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's marriage to Sangili Ammaiyar is a love marriage, which is called a natural marriage. It is a spontaneous union, without the efforts of a secret love or a chaste love, which are discussed in Tamil Akapporul (Tamil love poetry) texts. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions it here as "by the ancient decree." The second type of marriage, the ordained marriage, is when the father and mother give the girl in marriage with rituals and ceremonies. Therefore, as the time ordained by the Lord arrived, one day, Nambi Arurar, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, departed from his sacred mansion and entered the Lord's temple. The 225th verse: "The Lord of the celestials, who is a Brahmin, ruled Nambi. He worshipped the Lord with the beautiful eyes in the ancient manner, sang praises, and came out. He saw the sacred services performed by the devotees, worshipped them, and proceeded. He entered the sacred flower pavilion, which resembled a lotus pond." The Lord of all gods, Shiva, took the form of an old Brahmin and directly enslaved Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, who resided in Thiruvottriyur and worshipped Lord Shiva daily in the prescribed manner, entered the temple as usual on that day, worshipped Lord Shiva in the prescribed manner, sang praises, and came out. He came to the outer circumambulatory path outside the Lord's mansion. There, he saw and worshipped the sacred services performed for the Lord. This implies that even the sacred services performed for the Lord are worthy of being seen and worshipped. Therefore, the sacred services performed for the Lord were taking place in the outer circumambulatory path of the temple. These included sacred garden work, sweeping the sacred courtyard, polishing sacred vessels, lamps, etc., and performing all the cleaning and service work. These are the sacred services of Chariyai (external worship). These sacred services, appropriate for each type of work, take place in various places, from the outer circumambulatory path. Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal proceeded, worshipping all these sacred services.

Then, he entered the sacred flower pavilion, which is called Thiruppushpa Mandapam, resembling a lotus pond. Many kinds of flowers were gathered there. It was cool and filled with water everywhere. Therefore, that sacred flower pavilion was like a lotus pond. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal entered that sacred flower pavilion. The 226th verse: "The devotees, whose love was like a thread, strung the five letters (Panchaaksharam) in their hearts, and made garlands of flowers. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped these devotees, who were firm in their inner devotion, and moved to another place. As before, he removed the screen and gave the flowers to be offered to the Lord. He then saw Sangiliyar, who disappeared like lightning, by divine decree." In that sacred flower pavilion, devotees were making garlands of flowers. What kind of devotees were they? The devotees were chanting the Sri Panchaaksharam (five-letter mantra) in their hearts with unwavering love, counting the beads, and making garlands of flowers without speaking. This is the rule for making garlands of flowers. In the Thirupuranam of Eripattha Nayanar, we saw that Sivakami Andar plucked flowers in the sacred garden with her mouth covered with a cloth. All these are included in the Pushpa Vidhis (rules for flowers). According to these rules, as stated in the Shivagamas, devotees were making garlands of flowers here. Love is the thread, and the flower strung on it is the Sri Panchaaksharam. Therefore, one should constantly chant and meditate on the Sri Panchaaksharam in the heart. While doing so, one should make garlands of flowers with one's hands. Thus, the devotees were performing the sacred flower service in that sacred flower pavilion. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped those devotees. We saw that even the Lord's sacred services are worthy of being seen and worshipped. Similarly, here, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal worshipped the devotees who were making garlands of flowers. As he worshipped and came, there was a private place inside that sacred flower pavilion. It was covered with a screen. It was a private place where no one else could see the work being done inside. It was surrounded by screens. Women would perform the sacred flower work from behind that screen. Once it was completed, they would remove the screen, bring the garlands to be offered to the Lord, give them to the devotees there, and then quickly go back behind the screen. As Sundaramoorthy Swamigal approached that private place, Sangili Ammaiyar took all the garlands she had made, removed the screen, came out, gave the garlands to the devotees to be offered to the Lord, and then quickly went back behind the screen, like a flash of lightning. As she came and went, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal saw Sangili Ammaiyar by divine grace. The next three verses are 227, 228, and 229.

"When the sacred devotee, who had a bull banner, saw her, who was like an unstrung pearl and a tender bud, his mind, which was not guarded, went to her. The arrows of Kama, which had been abandoned by him, came and struck him. He, who was unable to bear it, came out and spoke, 'It is difficult to know what kind of person this is. Inside the screen, in a corner, is she like a lightning creeper, made of gold and jewels, mixed with the light of nectar, and molded with the coolness of the new moon? Who is she who has turned my heart?' As he spoke, those standing nearby replied, 'She is the maiden Sangiliyar. She is a maiden who performs the Lord's service with abundant penance.' He then realized, 'The Lord made me attain this birth by the grace of two women. One is Paravai, and this is the other.' Thus, he was bewildered." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal saw Sangili Ammaiyar by the grace of the Lord. This is one of the Akapporul (love poetry) themes called Kaatchi (sight). We saw this theme of Kaatchi occurring with Paravaiyar in Thiruvallur in the Thaduthaatkonda Puranam. Here too, a similar Kaatchi occurs. This is also a continuation of the sight they had in Thirukailash and then separated. As soon as Sundaramoorthy Swamigal saw Sangili Ammaiyar, his mind went to Sangili Ammaiyar. As he was in this state, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal came out of the temple. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal asked about the feelings he had. To this, those standing nearby replied, "She is the maiden Sangiliyar. Sangili Ammaiyar is one who performs the Lord's service with abundant penance." At that time, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal thought in his sacred heart, "The Lord made me attain this birth by the grace of two women. Among those two women, Paravai, whom I have already married, is one, and this Sangiliyar is the other woman, the second woman." Thus, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal was bewildered. His question, "Who is she?" is the theme of Aiyam (doubt) in Akapporul. The scriptures state that the Lord granting birth is also His grace, as it helps to experience and exhaust karmas and attain liberation. But here, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's birth and sacred incarnation are not merely for the sake of these two women, Paravaiyar and Sangiliyar. The purpose of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's sacred incarnation is also for the southern land, which performed great penance, to flourish, and for the Thiruthondar Thogai (collection of sacred devotees) to be given. That is why the divine grace made Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's mind go to those women in Thirukailash. As a result of that, all these great sacred histories occur. We must understand this. Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, Sangili Ammaiyar, and Paravai Nachiyar's sacred incarnation is not like the birth of beings like us, which is due to karma. They were born here to make the southern land, which performed great penance, flourish, and to give the blameless Thiruthondar Thogai and Thiruppathigam (sacred hymns) so that Shiva devotion and devotee devotion may prosper. For this, the divine grace of the Lord makes these two Ammaiyars a cause. We must understand this.

We will continue to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 873, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkaama Nayanar Puranam. After seeing Sangili Ammaiyar, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal enters the temple, thinking, "I will ask the Lord for Sangili and receive her." The 230th verse: "He entered, thinking, 'I, who live by the decree of being the servant of the Lord with the lightning-like matted hair, am prevented by this Sangili Ammaiyar's penance from attaining the blessings that come from His grace. She binds my life and beautiful flowers together. I will receive her from the Lord with the golden Konrai flowers on His head.'" The Lord, Shiva, has already made Sundaramoorthy Swamigal His servant, separating him from all worldly connections. Therefore, everything that happens to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal happens by Shiva's grace. It is proper to ask Shiva for all these things that Shiva has shown and brought together. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal has already stated in his Thevaram, "I have placed my mind only on your sacred feet, without any other attachment," and "I consider you as my wealth and true treasure." These are the states of Shiva's life that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal embraced. Therefore, he went to Shiva, thinking, "I will receive her from Shiva." In reality, it is Lord Shiva who brings about all the experiences and karmic fruits that come to all living beings. But all these beings, unaware of this truth, are deluded by the veil of ego and think that all these things come from their own efforts. But enlightened souls like Sundaramoorthy Swamigal are those who have fully realized the truth that everything comes from Lord Shiva. Therefore, they lived, knowing that Shiva is the giver and He is the Lord. Now, the Lord Himself has said to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, "We have given you friendship," and has accepted Sundaramoorthy Swamigal as a friend. We saw this in the Thaduthaatkonda Puranam. Therefore, Sivakavimani Aiyya has commented that this is also appropriate in the context of Paangar Kuttam (meeting of friends), one of the themes in Tamil literature. Thus, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal enters the Thiruvottriyur temple. The 231st verse: "He worshipped the luminous Supreme Being, who is the Lord of Thiruvottriyur, who is not known by Brahma on the lotus or by Vishnu, who delved into the sky and earth, who has a sacred head adorned with the growing crescent moon and long anklets, and who, though He owns all the worlds, lovingly resides in Thiruvottriyur, and stood before Him and praised Him." The Lord of Thiruvottriyur is He who is not known by Brahma on the lotus or by Vishnu, who delved into the sky and earth. The Lord of Thiruvottriyur has a sacred head adorned with the growing crescent moon and long anklets. Though He owns all the worlds, He lovingly resides in Thiruvottriyur. This is the unique specialty of Thiruvottriyur. Although the Lord is pervasive throughout the world, He remains hidden there like ghee in milk. In supreme sacred places and Shiva temples, He shines forth like ghee in curd, says the Gnana Sasthiram. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to this with the phrase, "though He owns all the worlds, He lovingly resides in Thiruvottriyur, the luminous light." Amarthal means to reside lovingly. "He shines brightly in some places and not in others," says the 12th Sutra of Sivagnana Botham. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, who goes before such a Lord of Thiruvottriyur, makes a request to the Lord for Sangili Ammaiyar. That is the next verse. The 232nd verse: "O Lord of Thiruvottriyur, you rejoice in having Uma Ammaiyar on one side, and you lovingly conceal Mother Ganga in your long, sacred matted hair. You, who are so greatly desirous, please give me Sangili, whose face is like the moon, who makes garlands for you and unties the knots of my heart, and relieve my suffering." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal says to the Lord, "O Lord of Thiruvottriyur, you rejoice in having Uma Ammaiyar on one side. Not only that, but you have also lovingly concealed Mother Ganga in your long, sacred matted hair. You are so greatly desirous. You, who are so greatly desirous, please give me Sangili, who makes garlands for you and unties the knots of my heart, and relieve my suffering." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal was already married to Paravai Nachiyar and living with her. He is asking the Lord for another wife, Sangiliyar, even though he already has Paravaiyar as his wife. If the Lord were to ask, "You are already married to Paravaiyar. Do you want to marry Sangiliyar too?" Sundaramoorthy Swamigal replies to the Lord beforehand, "You have Uma Ammaiyar on your left side, and you have concealed another woman in your matted hair. I also desire the same. If that state is suitable for you, it is also suitable for me." Thus, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal asks the Lord in a friendly manner. We can remember here that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is a friend of the Lord, and the Lord Himself desired friendship and gave it to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal showed the path of Sakamargam (path of friendship) to this world. The reason for the Lord concealing Ganga was love. Similarly, here too, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal indicates that love is the reason. When speaking about Sangili Ammaiyar, he says, "She makes garlands for you. At the same time, Sangiliyar is also capable of untying the knots of my heart." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal says that Sangiliyar has renounced all her relatives and attachments and has become your property. Therefore, only you can give her to me. You are the only one worthy of giving her. Thus, he makes a request to the Lord, "Therefore, give me Sangiliyar and relieve my suffering." This is what Sundaramoorthy Swamigal requested from the Lord with his sacred words, standing before the Lord. The 233rd verse: "After making many requests to the Lord, knowing that He knows all, he came out. He thought, 'Sangiliyar has stolen all the firmness of my heart, which always thinks of being your servant. I do not know what to do now. O Lord with the cool moon and coral-like matted hair, please bestow your grace upon me,' and he grew weary." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, after making many sweet requests to the Lord, knowing that the Lord knows all, came out of the temple. He then thought to the Lord, "O Lord, Sangiliyar has stolen all the firmness of my heart, which always thinks of being your servant. I do not know what to do now. O Lord with the cool moon and coral-like matted hair, please bestow your grace upon me," and he grew weary. Although the Lord knows everything as it is, this verse says that he made requests to the Lord, knowing that He knows all. Making such requests to the Lord, knowing that He knows all, serves to strengthen and mature the love one has for Him. Nambigal's complaint to the Lord is also for the benefit of instructing the people of the world. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal says, "I have placed it in you." The verse says, "My heart always thinks of being your servant." We see all these sacred words in Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's Thevaram, "I have placed my heart in you," and "I have placed my head, tongue, and heart in you without any deceit." What does it mean to think of being a servant of the Lord? It means to constantly keep the heart in a state of Shiva Yoga. "Even if I forget, I will say 'Namah Shivaya,'" says Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. Nambigal practiced Shiva Yoga in such a way that even his external senses were trained in this state of Shiva Yoga. In the Thiruppathigam of Thiruaamathur, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal explains the Shiva Yoga he practiced, saying, "I will seek, I will seek, four fingers above the navel." Thirugnanasambandha Peruman says, "I, who cannot forget." Thirunavukkarasu Peruman has sung, "I think, what shall I say I think? I have no eyes but to think of the sacred feet of my Lord." Our Paramacharyas have thus taught us. Therefore, living by constantly remembering that Lord Shiva is our Lord, that we are His eternal servants, and that He is the greatly compassionate one who bestows His grace upon us at every moment, even if we make mistakes, is the only way to attain salvation. Our Paramacharyas have thus shown us. Did Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's mind, which always thought of Shiva's service, go to something else here? That too was brought about by Shiva's grace, by divine decree. It is to be understood that Nambigal's mind would not go anywhere outside of Shiva. Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's decision to receive her from Lord Shiva, and his standing before Lord Shiva and requesting, confirm his state of Shiva Yoga. In this verse, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal requests and calls upon the Lord, "O Lord who wears the moon in your matted hair." The Lord wearing the crescent moon signifies that the Lord is the embodiment of grace, who protects and nurtures any soul that takes refuge in Him and comes to Him in distress. That is the significance of Him wearing the moon in His matted hair. Similarly, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal here takes refuge in the Lord, saying, "I have taken refuge in you. Please protect my life." This is the inner meaning of his request to the Lord. We will continue to contemplate. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 874, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkama Nayanar Puranam. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, after praying to the Lord in the temple and requesting Sangili Ammaiyar, now comes out of the temple.

The 234th verse: "Mathi vaazh mudiyar magizh koyil purathu or marungu vandhu iruppa Kathiron melaikkadal kaana maalaikkadalai kandu ayarvaar muthiraa mulaiyaar thammai manam punarkka vendi mularri valai nidhiyaan nanbar thamakku arulum nanbaal ninaindhu ninaindhu azhiya enbadhu thiruppaadal."

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is now staying on one side outside the temple where the Lord resides. This is not the usual residence where Sundaramoorthy Swamigal stays in Thiruvottriyur. This is a private place where Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is staying next to the temple. It is evening, and the sun is setting in the west. This evening time is a period of sorrow for those separated from their companions. This is beautifully explained in Tamil literature within the various aspects of Akapporul (love poetry). At that time, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal melts in thought, wishing that the Lord would arrange his marriage to Sangili. The Lord is a friend of Kubera (the god of wealth), who possesses the two treasures, Sanghanidhi and Padmanidhi. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prays to the Lord, asking Him to help him through the friendship that the Lord has not only with Kubera but also with him.

The verse: "Umbar uyya ulaguyya ola velai vidamunda thambiranaar vanthondar thambaal eythi Sangiliyai imbar ulagil yaavarukkum eythavonna irundhavaththu kombai unakku tharugindrom konda kavalai oli enna enbadhu thiruppaadal."

As Sundaramoorthy Swamigal makes that request to the Lord in the evening, the Lord, who consumed poison to save the heavens and the earth, appears before Nambi (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal). The Lord appears before Nambi and says, "I give you Sangili, who is of great penance, unattainable by anyone in this world. Therefore, cast away the sorrow you hold in your heart." The Lord thus graciously tells Sundaramoorthy Swamigal.

The idea here is that the Lord consumed poison for the salvation of the Devas (celestial beings) and the people of this world. Similarly, as a result of the impending marriage between Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and Sangili Ammaiyar, the Devas and the people of the world are to receive divine grace. This is the implication. The Lord appears directly before Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and says this. The greatness of Sangili Ammaiyar is expressed here through the very words of the Lord. If the Lord Himself says that Sangiliyar is one who has performed great penance that no one else can achieve, then the greatness of Sangili Ammaiyar's profound penance is conveyed to us here. Therefore, to be worthy of marrying such a greatly ascetic Sangili Ammaiyar, one must possess even greater penance than Sangili Ammaiyar.

That Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is one who possesses such superior penance is confirmed in the following verse. The 236th verse: "Andru vennainalluril valiya aandukondu aruli ondrum ariyaa naayenukku urudhi aliththeer uyir kaakka indrum ivalai manam punarkku nindreer ena potri mandral malarchevadi inai keezh vanangi magizhndhaar vanthondar."

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal melts in thought, remembering that the Lord Himself appeared directly and promised to give Sangili to him. He praises the Lord, saying, "On that day in Thiruvannainallur, you forcibly took me into your service; that was the power of your great grace." He continues, "You came forcibly in Thiruvannainallur and took me, a dog who knows nothing, into your service, and gave me assurance to protect my life. Today, you have consented to arrange this marriage for Sangili and have bestowed your grace upon me." Thus, praising the Lord, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal rejoices, bowing at the Lord's lotus feet. Throughout the life story of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, we see the event of divine grace where the Lord Himself came forcibly and took him into service in Thiruvannainallur. When Sundaramoorthy Swamigal denied, "I am not your servant," the Lord forcibly came and argued in the marriage pandal (marriage hall), saying, "This one is my servant." That marriage was a marriage that was to happen under the illusion of worldly circumstances. At that time, the Lord, our Lord, came and took Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, who was standing as the groom there, into service, preventing him from getting involved in that marriage and going into worldly life. He won the case in Vennainallur, disappeared, and then appeared on the Rishabha (bull mount), enlightening Sundaramoorthy Swamigal about the truth as it is, and took him into service.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal rejoiced, considering it the Lord's great grace. The Lord separated Sundaramoorthy Swamigal from worldly illusion and followed him to take him into service. That was the boon given in Thirukailayam (Mount Kailash), and that alone is the assurance for life. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal realized that this marriage was to happen as a continuation of that same boon received in Thirukailayam and the command received there. Therefore, he praises the Lord, saying, "On that day, you gave assurance in Thirukailayam. According to that, first, you came and stopped me in Thiruvannainallur. Now, here, you have promised to give Sangili Ammaiyar to me." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal rejoices, bowing at the Lord's lotus feet. The 237th verse: "Aandu konda andhananaar avarukku aruli karunaiyinaal neenda kangu yamaththu neengi vaanil nirai madhiyam theendu kanni maadaththu sendru thigazh Sangiliyaaraam thoondusothi vilakkanaiyaar thambaal kanavil thondrinaar."

The Lord, the Brahmin who took Sundaramoorthy Swamigal into service, just as He graced Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, now leaves that place in the night and goes to the Kannimaadam (maiden's chamber) where Sangili Ammaiyar is staying. Here, saying that the Lord appeared to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal and then left to go to the Kannimaadam where Sangili Ammaiyar is, is merely a figure of speech. Because for the Lord, going and coming are not applicable in that sense. He is omnipresent, pervading everywhere. All other things are contained within His pervasiveness. Therefore, He is the Punnian (meritorious one) who has no going, coming, or union. So, when it says that the Lord left Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's place and went to the Kannimaadam, it should be understood as the Lord manifesting and then disappearing, or manifesting and then concealing Himself. Thus, going to the Kannimaadam, the Lord appears in the dream of Sangiliyar, who is like a kindled lamp of light. "Thoondusothi vilakku anaiyaar" means a lamp of light that shines brightly, illuminating the minds of the people of this world and inspiring good in them. Another meaning is that it is a lamp that is now to be kindled and shine by the Lord. In the dream of such a Sangili Ammaiyar, the Lord appears. There are many ways in which the Lord manifests and reveals Himself to souls for their grace. Among the three types of souls – Vijnanakalar, Pralayakalar, and Sakalar – the Lord appears to Vijnanakalar in their own nature, as the knowledge within their knowledge. To Pralayakalar, the Lord appears directly before them. To Sakalar, who are ordinary souls, He appears and reveals Himself in indirect ways, such as in the form of a Guru. Additionally, the Lord reveals Himself to the graced ones in dreams and in waking states. We see this in the words of the Thirumurais (sacred hymns). The Thevaram of Thirugnanasambandha Peruman says, "Kanavilum enakku vandhu eythu nirmalan" (The pure one who comes to me even in dreams). The Thiruvaimoor Pathigam of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman contains the meaning, "Unni unni urangugindrenukku thannai vaaimoor thalaivanaama solli" (To me who sleeps thinking and thinking, He revealed Himself as the Lord of Vaimoor). The Thiruvachagam says, "Kanavilum devarkku ariyaay potri nanavilum naayarkku arulinai potri" (Praise to you who are rare even to the Devas in dreams, praise to you who grace even dogs in waking). Therefore, through these sacred words, it is understood that the Lord reveals Himself in dream states and waking states. The Lord also reveals Himself as an ethereal voice, as a pervasive light in the sky. He also comes and graces in many other divine forms. The Lord's manifestation in these various states occurs according to the individual's state and maturity. We should not see differences or hierarchies in these ways the Lord manifests. Thirugnanasambandha Peruman's divine command is, "Aatpaal avarkku arulum vannamum aadhi maanbum ketpaan pugil alavillai kilakka vendaa" (If one attempts to inquire into the manner of His grace to His servants and His primordial greatness, it is boundless and need not be spoken of). Therefore, in these ways of revealing, the Lord appears to Sangili Ammaiyar in a dream.

The 238th and 239th verses are as follows: "Thotrum pozhudhil Sangiliyar thozhudhu vizhundhu paravasamaay aatra anbu pongi ezhundhu adiyen uyya ezhundharulum peetru en yaan seyvadhu ena periya karunai pozhindhanaiya neetrukkola vedhiyarum ner nindru arulai seygindrar. Saarum thavaththuch Sangili kel saala enpaal anbu udaiyaan meruvaraiyin mempattath thavaththaan vennai nallooril yaarum ariya yaan aazha uriyaan unnai ena irandhaan vaarkonmulaiyaay nee avanai manaththaal anaivaay magizhndhu endraar enbavai thiruppaadalgal."

The Lord appears in Sangili Ammaiyar's dream. When Sangiliyar sees the Lord in her dream, she bows down to the ground, becomes ecstatic, and overflows with immense love. The form in which the Lord appeared in Sangili Ammaiyar's dream was that of a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash, overflowing with compassion. Sekkizhar Peruman highlights that divine form here as "karunai pozhindhanaiya neetrukkola vedhiyar" (a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash, as if compassion itself was overflowing). This very form of a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash is the form the Lord showed to Thirunavukkarasu Peruman in Thirumaraikkadu, the form shown in Thirukailayam, to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal in Thiruvannainallur, and to Thiruvathavooradigal. And now, the Lord appears in a dream to Sangili Ammaiyar in the same form. This form of a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash seems to be a familiar and ancient form for the Lord. Bowing to the Lord who appeared in this manner, Sangili Ammaiyar says, "What can I, your servant, do in return for the great blessing of your coming to save me?" The Lord, who appeared as a Brahmin adorned with sacred ash, as if great compassion was overflowing, then graciously speaks to Sangili Ammaiyar. The overflowing sacred ash on the Brahmin form of the Lord is like the immense, unmanifested compassion within the Lord overflowing and unable to be contained. With such a form, the Lord tells Sangili Ammaiyar, "Listen, Sangili, who possesses profound penance that seeks me! He is one who has great love for me, and he is of penance greater than Mount Meru. In Thiruvannainallur, I took him as my servant for all to see. He asked me for you. Therefore, Sangili, you shall marry him with joy in your heart."

The fact that Sangili Ammaiyar is one who possesses penance that seeks the Lord comes from the Lord's own words. Thirukkural says, "Saarbu unarndhu saarbu keda ozhugin" (If one understands the attachment and acts to destroy it). Penance is performed towards Lord Shiva. Sekkizhar Peruman refers to Sangiliyar's penance as "saarum thavam" (seeking penance) to indicate that it is penance that seeks the Lord, eliminating all other forms of penance. The Lord Himself, through His words, calls Sangili Ammaiyar "saarum thavaththu Sangili" (Sangili of seeking penance), indicating that she is full of penance. Similarly, when speaking of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, He says that he is of penance greater than Mount Meru. Therefore, the states and connections of both of them arise from their Shiva-seeking penance. Their marriage occurs due to their Shiva-seeking connection. It is not a marriage that occurs due to worldly connections, like the marriages of other worldly people. To convey that considering it so would be a transgression, the Lord Himself refers to Sangili Ammaiyar as "saarum thavaththu Sangili" and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal as "meruvaraiyin mempattath thavaththaan" (one of penance greater than Mount Meru). We must understand this as it is. Therefore, the Lord graciously tells Sangili Ammaiyar, "You shall marry that Vanthondan (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal) according to custom and live happily. Accept him with a joyful heart, and after living happily, you shall come to our world, Thirukailayam." We will continue to contemplate this.

Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 875, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkama Nayanar Puranam. The three continuous verses, 240, 241, and 242, are as follows: "When the Primeval Lord stood before her and blessed her, Sangiliyar, whose beauty even Vishnu and Brahma could not comprehend, fell at his cool, lotus-like feet, and then stood up before the Primeval Lord of the Vedas, trembling, and worshipped him, saying, 'O my Lord, I am worthy of your blessing. O Lord of the celestials, I have accepted your divine command. When you graciously give me to Nambi Aruran in a proper ritualistic marriage, I have a request to make to you, who hold Uma, the creeper of the Himalayas, in one part of your body.'"

"Then, before the Lord with matted hair, she, greatly shy, bowed and said, 'O Lord, who wears the shining sacred thread on your chest, touched by the breasts of our Lady, you know that he (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal) delights greatly in Thiruvārur. Please bless me accordingly.'" These are the verses. Lord Shiva, the Primeval Lord, tells Sangili Ammaiyar, "Accept Nambi Aruran." As soon as the Primeval Lord blessed her, the beautiful Sangili Ammaiyar bows down at the cool, lotus-like feet of Lord Shiva, whom even Vishnu and Brahma cannot comprehend. She falls down and then stands up before the Primeval Lord of the Vedas, trembling, and worships him.

The word "sennindru" in the verse means "standing straight." This implies the custom of standing straight before the Lord and during Shiva Puja. It is mentioned that she worships, trembling. It is as if she is informing the Lord of something he does not know. Now, Sangili Ammaiyar begins to pray to the Lord. Therefore, she trembled. Even though the Lord knows everything, she trembles when she begins to reply to him. Even though Sangiliyar knows fully well that the Lord knows what is to be desired, she is about to pray to the Lord out of eagerness. Therefore, she trembled. Thus, Sangili Ammaiyar prays to the Lord, trembling. "O my Lord, I am worthy of him whom you have blessed.

O Lord of the celestials, I accept your divine command with reverence. When you graciously give me to Nambi Aruran in a proper ritualistic marriage, I have a request to make to you, who hold Uma, the creeper of the Himalayas, in one part of your body," says Sangili Ammaiyar. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal was blessed by you. This marriage was blessed by Lord Shiva in Kailash before. Here, he also appears in a dream and blesses. Among the two types of marriages, Kalavu Manam (secret marriage) and Karpu Manam (chaste marriage), Lord Shiva is about to give Sangili Ammaiyar to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal openly, with the knowledge of the village and relatives. Thus, Sangili Ammaiyar is to be given to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal by the Lord of Thiruvottiyur, who is the special authority here, with the knowledge of the village and relatives.

Now, a formal marriage is about to take place. Therefore, this is a marriage that falls under the category of "vidhi manam" (a marriage ordained by fate or divine will). Sangili Ammaiyar left her parents, village, and relatives and placed herself under the grace of Lord Shiva. Therefore, the right to perform Sangili Ammaiyar's marriage, both generally and specifically, fell to the Lord of Thiruvottiyur. It became the duty of the Lord of Thiruvottiyur. Therefore, Sangili Ammaiyar prays to the Lord, saying, "When you graciously give me." "You always remain inseparable from Uma, holding her in one part of your body. Similarly, Nambi Aruran, who is to be my husband, should always remain with me, inseparable." This is the request she is about to make. Accordingly, she addresses the Lord as "O Lord, who holds Uma in one part of your body," and makes her request.

Sangili Ammaiyar continues to say to the Lord, "O Lord, Nambi Aruran, who is Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, is one who delights greatly and permanently resides in Thiruvārur. You should know that quality and bless me accordingly." Sangili Ammaiyar, who is like an unfading lamp, makes this request to the Lord. Sekkizhar Peruman mentions "peruga naani" (greatly shy) when she makes this request. Shyness is the first of the four natural qualities of womanhood. It is a natural quality of womanhood to desire that her husband should always remain with her, inseparable, and exclusively hers. But when she expresses this to others, that shyness, which is characteristic of womanhood, comes into play. Moreover, the nature of expressing things indirectly, without being able to state them openly, is a manifestation of that shyness. Therefore, what is Sangili Ammaiyar requesting from the Lord here? Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, after marrying her, should never leave her. This is the desire that Sangili Ammaiyar holds in her heart. She does not express this desire openly to the Lord. Instead, she expresses it indirectly, saying that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is always fond of staying in Thiruvārur, so the Lord should bless her in a way that is appropriate for his nature. Sangili Ammaiyar expresses this request indirectly.

"Delighting greatly in Thiruvārur" is Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's nature. Therefore, if he goes to Thiruvārur after marriage, separation will occur. Moreover, he is the husband of another lady, Paravai Nachiyar, in Thiruvārur. Therefore, Sangili Ammaiyar indirectly conveys to the Lord the condition that he should not leave her after marriage. The Lord, who knows everything, also knows the inner thoughts of Sangili Ammaiyar. Nevertheless, out of eagerness, Sangili Ammaiyar makes this request, and her body trembles. She is like an unfading lamp, an undiminishing, unwaning lamp. The three verses, 243, 244, and 245, are as follows: "The Lord who resides in Thiruvottiyur, having understood the state of Vanthondar (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal) from her words, blessed her, saying, 'O lady with golden bangles, he will make a vow to you that he will not leave you. He will make a vow in a secret manner.' Thus, having blessed her, he returned from the maiden's chamber and went to his friend, who was joyful, and said, 'We have told her your desire to marry her. There is a condition that you must fulfill for her to marry you.' Vanthondar, delighted, bowed and asked, 'What is the duty I must perform?' And he was told, 'Go to her now, this very night, and make a vow that you will not leave her, so that you may marry her.'" These are the verses. The Lord, who resides in Thiruvottiyur, accepted all the words that Sangili Ammaiyar prayed.

The Lord, having accepted Sangiliyar's request, also knew the state of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's mind. What was Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's state of mind or inner desire? It was Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's life to go to all the temples where the Lord resided, worship him, and sing his praises. The Lord also knew this. Generally, "aruli" (blessing) refers to the Lord's special awareness that he undertakes by activating his power to operate knowledge, desire, and action. Therefore, the Lord of Thiruvottiyur, having understood Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's state of mind, now blesses Sangili Ammaiyar. He calls Sangili Ammaiyar and says, "O Sangili, adorned with golden bangles, Nambi Aruran will make a vow to you that he will not leave you. He will make a vow in a secret manner between the two of you." The Lord blesses Sangili Ammaiyar in this way.

Having blessed her thus, the Lord returns from Sangiliyar and comes to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal. The Lord comes to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, his joyful friend, and says, "We have told her your desire to marry her. There is a condition that you must fulfill for her to marry you. If you do that, you can marry her," says the Lord. Nambigal's heart desired to marry Sangili Ammaiyar, but Sekkizhar Peruman clearly states here that it was a pure heart. Sekkizhar Peruman, having researched why Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, who had already married Paravai Nachiyar, now desired to marry Sangili Ammaiyar, and to prevent those who read and hear this story from hastily committing sacrilege and suffering, mercifully warns and states in this verse that Nambigal's heart was pure and unblemished.

To reveal that his heart was pure and unblemished, he uses the phrase "thūya manam" (pure heart). He was a friend of the Lord. The Lord, who was such a friend, says to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, "If you want to marry her, you must do one thing. If you do that, she is ready to accept you. She gives her consent," says the Lord. Immediately, Vanthondar (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal), delighted, bows and asks the Lord, "What is the action I must perform?" To that, the Lord says, "Before you marry her, you must give her a promise. You must vow before her, this very night, that you will not leave Sangiliyar and will stay with her." The Lord blesses him. Hearing that, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal says to the Lord, "To perform this marriage, if this marriage is to take place, I will do whatever action is required for this marriage to take place. But for that, I must receive your divine grace." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prays to the Lord. We will continue to contemplate what Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prays to the Lord. Thiruchitrambalam.

Thiruchitrambalam. Sekkizhar Peruman's Periya Puranam, Part 876, Vampara Vari Vandu Sarukkam, Eyarkon Kalikkama Nayanar Puranam. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal gives an assurance to the Lord that he is ready to do whatever is necessary to marry Sangiliyar. The 246th verse says: "If this can be achieved, I will do it. For that, O Lord with the lightning-like matted hair, I need your grace," he said. The Primeval Lord, with a smile, looked at his face and said, "What more do you need for that action?" This is how the verse is structured. The Lord said, "If you want to marry her, you must vow to her that you will always stay here with her and never leave her." To this, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal replied,

"I will do whatever action will make this marriage happen, but first, I must receive your divine grace," Sundaramoorthy Swamigal says to the Lord. To that, the Lord, with a faint smile, looks at Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's face and asks, "What more do you need to make that vow?" It is not customary to make a vow and then marry. It is not customary to marry by giving a promise. Therefore, the Lord asks Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, "What more do you need?" It is Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's duty and responsibility to go to Sangili Ammaiyar, make a vow, and get married. Even so, Lord Shiva asks Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, "What more do you need to do?"

The 247th verse says: "Vanthondar (Sundaramoorthy Swamigal), who gave his heart to the maiden with soft, fragrant breasts, knew that his Lord would visit other holy places and worship the Lord in his desired forms. With the thought that this (vow) would be an obstacle to his duty, he prayed to his Lord, expressing his shortcoming." This is how the verse is structured. Vanthondar, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, who gave his heart to Sangiliyar, asks the Lord. With what intention does he ask? Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's duty is to visit all the holy places where the Lord resides and worship the Lord in the forms in which he resides there. If he makes a vow to Sangili Ammaiyar and promises to stay with her always in Thiruvottiyur, that vow will be an obstacle to his worshipping the Lord in other holy places.

Considering this in his heart, he prays to the Lord, expressing his shortcoming. "Sing in beautiful Tamil about me on earth," was the command given by the Lord to Sundaramoorthy Swamigal when he took him as his own. Considering the Lord's command to him to visit various holy places and sing hymns as his duty, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal visits various holy places and praises the Lord's forms. If he makes a promise to Sangili Ammaiyar, as she desired, that he will stay with her always in Thiruvottiyur, it will hinder his primary duty. Considering this in his heart, he prays to the Lord. At this point, Sivakavimani Desikanar, who is commenting, raises another subtle question and answers it.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal has a duty to visit holy places and sing praises to the Lord. So, can't he take Sangili Ammaiyar with him to all the holy places he visits and sing praises? Then, the vow would be fulfilled, and Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's primary duty of visiting holy places and singing praises to the Lord would also be fulfilled. This question might arise in our minds. If we ask, "Can't he take Sangiliyar with him to all the other holy places and worship?" it is not so. Doing so is an act that people like us, who are bound by worldly life, would do, writes Sivakavimani Desikanar. He further states that even before, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal had married Paravai Nachiyar. But if we look at Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's pilgrimages so far, we see that he went alone without taking Paravai Nachiyar with him.

Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's desire for both Sangiliyar and Paravaiyar was only to the extent that it would lead to their liberation in this worldly life, and he did not lead this married life like the worldly lives of other people. We must understand that his life was a Shiva life, and his incarnation and life were for the benefit of this world. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal incarnated here with two divine purposes: "to make the southern region, which performed great penance, flourish, and to give the faultless Thiruthondar Thogai (a collection of hymns about devotees)." The two marriages that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal performed took place only to the extent that they supported the purpose of his incarnation, and they were not like the lives of other worldly people. The Lord's intervention to stop the arranged marriage of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal with the daughter of Puthur Sadangavi Sivachariyar, which was to be like the worldly lives of other people, was also based on this idea. Therefore, we should not consider our great spiritual masters as one of the worldly people. We must understand that their lives are not like ours. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is now going to pray to the Lord.

Sundaramoorthy Swamigal is going to pray to the Lord that when he makes a vow to Sangili Ammaiyar that he will never leave her, the Lord should not be inside the temple but should be present under the Magizha tree outside the temple. This is also the inner meaning of Sundaramoorthy Swamigal's prayer. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal did not say this or ask for this with the intention of deceiving Sangili Ammaiyar or speaking falsely. Sivakavimani Desikanar writes a subtle commentary, saying that we must keep all this in mind when studying this sacred history. The 248th verse says: "The King of Tamil, bowing at Shankara's feet, says, 'When I come with that maiden to make a vow that I will not leave her, you should leave the temple and reside under the sacred Magizha tree.' Thus he bowed." This is the verse. In this verse, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prays to the Lord. He bows at Shankara's feet and prays. Shankara means one who brings happiness. The one who prays thus is Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, the King of Tamil. He says to the Lord, "O Lord, when I come to make a vow that I will not leave Sangili, you should leave the temple and reside under the Magizha tree outside the temple." Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prays. It is only for a very short time that I will come with Sangiliyar and make that vow. Therefore, during that time, the Lord should leave the sanctum sanctorum and reside under the Magizha tree. The Lord is omnipresent and pervades everywhere without any exclusion. He pervades all things, both inside and outside, in a subtle way. He contains all things within his pervasion. If such a great Lord is asked by Sundaramoorthy Swamigal to leave the Shiva Lingam and reside under the Magizha tree, it means that even though the Lord is generally omnipresent and pervades everywhere without exclusion, he specially manifests brightly in the Shiva Lingam. Just as milk is present throughout a cow's body but manifests at the udder, the Lord, though present in all things, manifests most specially in the Shiva Lingam, say the Agamas (scriptural texts). Therefore, what Sundaramoorthy Swamigal desires is that the Lord should not manifest brightly in the Shiva Lingam but should remain hidden. He should manifest specially and brightly under the Magizha tree. This is what Sundaramoorthy Swamigal prays for. If we interpret it otherwise, that he should leave the temple and be under the Magizha tree, it would contradict the Lord's divine quality of omnipresence, which is an essential and excellent quality, and it would become an impossible task for the Lord. Therefore, we must interpret it in this way. Some people might criticize this as an intention to deceive Sangiliyar. But that is not the case. Sundaramoorthy Swamigal was intent on worshipping the Lord in all the temples. Therefore, he prays in this way, thinking that this vow would hinder that primary purpose. Even if he makes such a vow, we will see that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal will undertake pilgrimages, disregarding the suffering that might come from breaking the vow and worshipping the Lord in the places where he resides. We will see in the coming history that Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, even though he was ready to wholeheartedly endure all the sufferings that would come from breaking the vow, considered visiting the Lord's temples as his primary goal and undertook pilgrimages. The 249th and 250th verses say: "When the friend of the Lord prayed thus, the Lord of the celestials agreed, saying, 'Nambi, we will do as you said.' And Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, praising him, said, 'O my Lord, what more can be difficult for me now?' And having received his grace, he came out, with his hands folded in salutation on his head. The Lord with the red matted hair, delighted with his play with his friend, or perhaps contemplating the greatness of Sangiliyar's hereditary devotion, returned in the deep darkness to speak reassuring words to her." These are the two verses. When Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, the friend of the Lord, prayed thus, the Lord of the celestials agreed. He blessed him, saying, "Nambi, we will do as you said." Therefore, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, greatly delighted, praises the Lord, saying, "O my Lord, there is nothing more that is difficult for me to attain." He comes out, with his hands folded in salutation on his head, having received his grace. At that time, Lord Shiva, delighted with his play with his friend, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, or perhaps contemplating the greatness of Sangili Ammaiyar's hereditary devotion, we do not know why, returns to Sangili Ammaiyar in her dream in the deep darkness, when all living beings are asleep. Sekkizhar Peruman has structured this verse as his own statement. Sekkizhar Peruman structures this verse, "thunju irul meelavum anainthar" (returned in the deep darkness), to convey that even when all living beings are asleep, the Lord, without sleeping, is intent on blessing those souls. "Praise be to you, who neither eat nor sleep," is the sacred saying of Thirunavukkarasu Peruman. All the actions that the Lord performs for living beings are the five divine functions (Panchakrityam), which are his divine play. All the divine plays that the Lord performs are for the benefit of living beings. The Thirugnanasiddhiyar verse says: "What is the reason for these actions that are said to be performed? If one considers their origin, it is the play of the Primeval Lord. It is also said that he grants lasting intelligence and liberation to souls and, by his grace, removes all dense impurities." Now, the action that the Lord is about to perform is either for the sake of playing a divine game with his friend, Sundaramoorthy Swamigal, or to reveal to the world the greatness of Sangili Ammaiyar's devotion. Sekkizhar Peruman raises these two questions here and leaves it to the readers of this book to infer the answer. Sekkizhar Peruman's poetic excellence is evident in such places.
